label: Pump driver API and safety model

map.subsystem: Pump driver API and safety model (`plugins/pump-driver-api` = Gradle module `:pump-driver-api`, namespace `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.pump.api`) plus the `plugins/example` reference driver, and the platform-side enforcement in `:app` that the API contracts depend on (PluginRegistry, PluginEventBusImpl, RestrictedPluginContext, DexPluginLoader, SafetyLimitsStore, legacy adapters).

capabilities.name: Plugin base interface + lifecycle contract
capabilities.behavior: `interface Plugin`: vals `metadata: PluginMetadata`, `capabilities: Set<PluginCapability>`; methods `initialize(PluginContext)`, `shutdown()`, `onActivated()`, `onDeactivated()`, `settingsDescriptor(): PluginSettingsDescriptor`, `observeDashboardCards(): Flow<List<DashboardCardDescriptor>>`, `<T: PluginCapabilityInterface> getCapability(KClass<T>): T?`, plus two defaulted members: `observeDetailScreen(cardId): Flow<DetailScreenDescriptor>?` (default null) and `onDetailAction(cardId, actionKey)` (default no-op). Documented order: initialize once after factory creation (store context, no heavy work); onActivated when user selects it (start polling/auto-reconnect); onDeactivated when replaced/deactivated (stop work, KEEP credentials/settings); shutdown on destroy (release everything). Threading: lifecycle methods run on main thread and are serialized per-plugin by the registry lock; capability methods may be invoked from background dispatchers; settingsDescriptor/observeDashboardCards may be called on the UI thread.
edge_cases: initialize() throws -> plugin skipped entirely, never appears in available list, settings store entry removed
onActivated() throws -> activation fails, plugin stays inactive, Result.failure returned
onDeactivated() throws -> logged, deactivation continues anyway
shutdown() throws -> logged; registry only calls shutdown() on runtime-plugin removal, never for compile-time plugins

capabilities.name: DevicePlugin (hardware) extension
capabilities.behavior: `interface DevicePlugin : Plugin` adds `observeConnectionState(): StateFlow<ConnectionState>`; `connect(address: String, config: Map<String,String> = emptyMap())`; `disconnect()`; `scan(): Flow<DiscoveredDevice>`; and two defaulted members: `val pairingProfile: PairingProfile` (default `PairingProfile()` = CENTRAL_SCAN, advertisedName null) and `observePairingFault(): Flow<PairingFault?>` (default `flowOf(null)`). Contract in KDoc: connect MUST enforce a timeout, typically 30 seconds, and must not block indefinitely; disconnect must be a safe no-op when not connected; scan's flow completes when scanning ends (typically a timeout) and collectors cancel to stop early. `config` is a free-form string map; the platform adapter passes `"pairingCode"` (Tandem) and drivers may define their own (Medtronic reads `config["forceFirstPair"].toBoolean()`).
edge_cases: The 30s connect timeout is a documented convention only — nothing in the API enforces it
Medtronic ignores `address` entirely (phone is the peripheral); scan() emits a DiscoveredDevice only when a pump connects inbound

capabilities.name: ConnectionState machine
capabilities.behavior: `enum ConnectionState { DISCONNECTED, SCANNING, CONNECTING, AUTHENTICATING, AUTH_FAILED, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING }` (declared in PumpModels.kt). Nominal central-scan path: DISCONNECTED -> SCANNING (scan()) -> CONNECTING (connect()) -> AUTHENTICATING -> CONNECTED; auth rejection -> AUTH_FAILED; link loss from CONNECTED -> RECONNECTING -> CONNECTING/CONNECTED, or -> DISCONNECTED on give-up/explicit disconnect(). The enum itself encodes no transition table — each driver's connection manager owns transitions; the API only guarantees the state names and that the flow is a StateFlow (always has a current value). Advertise-and-wait plugins may never emit SCANNING and can stall without any transition at all, which is exactly why PairingFault exists as a parallel channel.
edge_cases: AUTH_FAILED is terminal-ish: no automatic path back without a new connect()
PumpDriverAdapter/PumpConnectionAdapter substitute DISCONNECTED whenever there is no active pump plugin

capabilities.name: PluginCapability enum and cardinality rules
capabilities.behavior: Seven values: GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, BGM_SOURCE, CALIBRATION_TARGET, DATA_SYNC, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER. `SINGLE_INSTANCE = {GLUCOSE_SOURCE, INSULIN_SOURCE, PUMP_STATUS, CALIBRATION_TARGET, BOLUS_CATEGORY_PROVIDER}` (max 1 active each); `MULTI_INSTANCE = {BGM_SOURCE, DATA_SYNC}` (many active). A companion `init` block runs `check(SINGLE_INSTANCE + MULTI_INSTANCE == entries.toSet())` and throws at class-load time listing any capability missing from both sets — an exhaustiveness guard that must be reproduced in Swift (e.g. a unit test or static assertion, since Swift has no enum-companion init). Capability declaration is purely the `Set<PluginCapability>` a plugin returns; the platform never introspects the driver otherwise. DATA_SYNC has NO capability interface yet — reserved, currently not implementable.
edge_cases: A plugin can declare a capability and return null from getCapability for it (the demo plugin does exactly this for DATA_SYNC) — declaration and implementation are not cross-checked

capabilities.name: Typed capability lookup (getCapability + as* helpers)
capabilities.behavior: `PluginCapabilityInterface` is an empty marker; every capability interface extends it. Lookup is `getCapability(type: KClass<T>): T?`, implemented in each driver as a `when(type)` over `GlucoseSource::class`/`InsulinSource::class`/`PumpStatus::class`/`BgmSource::class`/`CalibrationTarget::class`/`BolusCategoryProvider::class` returning `delegate as? T`, else null. Six extension functions on Plugin provide the sugar: `asGlucoseSource()`, `asInsulinSource()`, `asPumpStatus()`, `asBgmSource()`, `asCalibrationTarget()`, `asBolusCategoryProvider()`. Canonical implementation pattern: capability delegates are constructed in the plugin's constructor or `initialize()` as thin adapters over the BLE layer, keeping the plugin class limited to lifecycle + UI descriptors.
edge_cases: Kotlin KClass dispatch relies on unchecked casts (`@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")`); a Swift port needs a protocol-witness/type-keyed map instead
Requesting a capability the plugin declared but did not implement returns null, not an error

capabilities.name: PluginMetadata and PLUGIN_API_VERSION
capabilities.behavior: `const val PLUGIN_API_VERSION = 5` in PluginMetadata.kt. Documented history in the same comment: v3 renamed `BasalReading.controlIqMode` -> `activityMode` (PumpActivityMode enum); v4 added `BolusEvent.category` + the BolusCategoryProvider capability; v5 added the `getFullHistoryLogs()` overload to PumpDriver and PumpStatus. `data class PluginMetadata(id, name, version, apiVersion, description="", author="", iconResName: String?=null, protocolName: String?=null)`. Convention: `protocolName` + `version` render as e.g. "Tandem v1.0.0"; the plugin `version` doubles as the BLE-protocol version — there is deliberately no separate protocol-versioning infrastructure. Plugin IDs are reverse-domain and must match `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,127}$`. Bump the API version for breaking changes to Plugin/DevicePlugin, capability interfaces, PluginContext params, PluginEvent variants, SettingDescriptor/CardElement variants; additive changes do not require a bump.
edge_cases: docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md is stale: it says PLUGIN_API_VERSION is `2` (and the example README/plugin.json say `1`) while code says 5. The example plugin's META-INF/plugin.json declares apiVersion 1 and would therefore be REJECTED by DexPluginLoader today, even though DemoGlucometerFactory's Kotlin metadata uses PLUGIN_API_VERSION.

capabilities.name: PluginFactory and dual discovery
capabilities.behavior: `interface PluginFactory { val metadata: PluginMetadata; fun create(context: PluginContext): Plugin }`. Metadata must be available before instantiation so Settings can list plugins without creating them. Two discovery paths: (a) compile-time — factory is `@Singleton class X @Inject constructor(...)` bound via Hilt `@Binds @IntoSet` into `Set<PluginFactory>`, may inject dependencies (TandemPluginFactory injects BleConnectionManager, TandemBleDriver, BleScanner, TandemHistoryLogParser); (b) runtime — factory needs a public no-arg constructor and is instantiated reflectively from a sideloaded DEX JAR; it cannot use DI. The platform, not the factory, calls `plugin.initialize(context)` — `create()` receives the context but is expected to just build the instance. Tandem/Medtronic share one `METADATA` val between plugin and factory to avoid drift.
edge_cases: PluginRegistry calls both `factory.create(ctx)` and `plugin.initialize(ctx)` with the SAME context instance

capabilities.name: PluginContext (driver-facing platform services)
capabilities.behavior: `class PluginContext(androidContext: Context, pluginId: String, settingsStore: PluginSettingsStore, credentialProvider: PumpCredentialProvider, debugLogger: DebugLogger, eventBus: PluginEventBus, safetyLimits: StateFlow<SafetyLimits>, apiVersion: Int)`. `safetyLimits` is explicitly documented as a read-only constraint plugins must respect; drivers must read `.value` on every validation pass so backend updates apply immediately (rather than caching it at initialize()). `apiVersion` is always set to the platform's PLUGIN_API_VERSION. For compile-time plugins `androidContext` is the full Application context; for runtime plugins it is a restricted ContextWrapper (see sandbox capability). PluginContext is a plain class (not data class) — no equality/copy semantics relied upon.
edge_cases: The StateFlow instance is shared across all plugins — the registry mutates one `_safetyLimits` MutableStateFlow

capabilities.name: PluginSettingsStore (driver-facing key-value settings)
capabilities.behavior: Interface with paired getters/setters for four types, each getter taking a default: `getString(key, default="")/putString`, `getBoolean(key, default=false)/putBoolean`, `getInt(key, default=0)/putInt`, `getFloat(key, default=0f)/putFloat`, plus `remove(key)`. Implementation `PluginSettingsStoreImpl` is backed by `SharedPreferences("plugin_settings_$pluginId", MODE_PRIVATE)` and writes with `.apply()` (async commit; documented to callers as immediate/synchronous). Documented behaviors: settings survive deactivation and app updates, are namespaced per plugin ID, and are wiped on app uninstall; removing a runtime plugin explicitly calls `context.deleteSharedPreferences("plugin_settings_$pluginId")`. KDoc directs sensitive credentials to PumpCredentialProvider instead. The platform auto-persists values for Toggle/Slider/Dropdown/TextInput settings; ActionButton clicks are surfaced by the platform writing a timestamp to the button's key.
edge_cases: No type migration: reading a key with the wrong typed getter throws ClassCastException from SharedPreferences
Demo plugin uses the settings store as an ad-hoc IPC channel for detail-screen text input (reads KEY_DETAIL_BG_VALUE, then clears it)

capabilities.name: PumpCredentialProvider (driver-facing secret storage)
capabilities.behavior: Interface: `getPairedAddress(): String?`, `getPairingCode(): String?`, `isPaired(): Boolean`, `savePairing(address, pairingCode)`, `clearPairing()`, `saveJpakeCredentials(derivedSecretHex, serverNonceHex)`, `getJpakeDerivedSecret(): String?`, `getJpakeServerNonce(): String?`, `clearJpakeCredentials()`. Compile-time plugins get the app-wide implementation backed by EncryptedSharedPreferences. Runtime plugins get `ScopedCredentialProvider`, an isolated plain `SharedPreferences("plugin_creds_${sanitizeId(pluginId)}")` with keys `paired_address`, `pairing_code`, `jpake_derived_secret`, `jpake_server_nonce`; `sanitizeId` replaces `[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]` with `_` (deliberately preserving dots/hyphens/underscores so `com.foo.bar-baz` and `com.foo.bar.baz` stay distinct). `isPaired()` is defined as `prefs.contains(paired_address)`.
edge_cases: Documented decision: runtime plugins deliberately use UNencrypted SharedPreferences because they cannot access AndroidX Security; stated revisit trigger is 'if the threat model changes to include adversarial plugins, migration to EncryptedSharedPreferences is required'
Credentials readable via run-as on rooted/debug devices — accepted under the current trust model

capabilities.name: DebugLogger (BLE packet tracing)
capabilities.behavior: Interface with a nested `enum Direction { TX, RX }` and two methods: `logPacket(direction, opcode: Int, opcodeName: String, txId: Int, cargoHex: String, cargoSize: Int, parsedValue: String? = null, error: String? = null)` and `updateLastPacket(opcode, direction, parsedValue = null, error = null)` (for late-arriving parse results/errors on an already-logged packet). Security requirement in KDoc: implementations MUST retain raw packet data (cargoHex, parsedValue) only in debug/development builds and MUST never persist it to unencrypted storage, because these fields carry glucose readings, insulin doses and device identifiers. `HexUtils.toSpacedHex()` (`ByteArray.joinToString(" ") { "%02x".format(it.toInt() and 0xFF) }`) produces the canonical lowercase space-separated hex string used for cargoHex.
edge_cases: Runtime plugins get full unrestricted access to debugLogger

capabilities.name: SafetyLimits value type and hard bounds
capabilities.behavior: `data class SafetyLimits(minGlucoseMgDl: Int = 20, maxGlucoseMgDl: Int = 500, maxBasalRateMilliunits: Int = 15_000, maxBolusDoseMilliunits: Int = 25_000)`. Constants: DEFAULT_MIN_GLUCOSE=20, DEFAULT_MAX_GLUCOSE=500, DEFAULT_MAX_BASAL_MILLIUNITS=15_000 (15 U/hr, Tandem hardware max), DEFAULT_MAX_BOLUS_MILLIUNITS=25_000 (25 U single dose); the four ABSOLUTE_* constants are aliases of the DEFAULT_* values, so today defaults == absolute ceilings. The `init` block throws IllegalArgumentException unless: minGlucoseMgDl >= 20; maxGlucoseMgDl <= 500; minGlucoseMgDl < maxGlucoseMgDl; maxBasalRateMilliunits in 1..15_000; maxBolusDoseMilliunits in 1..25_000. Backend/user configuration may only NARROW the range, never widen it. Basal/bolus limits are in milliunits (integer); BolusEvent/BasalReading carry Float units — a ×1000 scale difference the port must preserve.
edge_cases: min==max is rejected (strict <)
19, -1, 501, basal 0 or 15_001, bolus 0 or 25_001 all throw
Documented revisit trigger: absolute bounds are Tandem-derived; OmniPod/Medtronic hardware with different physical limits may require revisiting the constants

capabilities.name: SafetyLimits.safeOf() lenient factory
capabilities.behavior: `safeOf(min=20, max=500, basal=15_000, bolus=25_000): SafetyLimits` clamps instead of throwing, for untrusted/backend input where a crash is worse than clamped values. Order matters: `clampedMin = min.coerceIn(20, 499)` (ABSOLUTE_MAX_GLUCOSE - 1); `clampedMax = max.coerceIn(clampedMin + 1, 500)`; `clampedBasal = basal.coerceIn(1, 15_000)`; `clampedBolus = bolus.coerceIn(1, 25_000)`. Consequence encoded in tests: `safeOf(min=450, max=300)` yields (450, 451) — the min wins and the max is pushed up, it does NOT swap them. `safeOf(bolus=0)` yields 1. The strict constructor is intentionally kept for programmatic callers; safeOf is the only path used for external data.
edge_cases: safeOf can silently produce a 1 mg/dL-wide valid window (450..451) from nonsensical config — no warning is logged

capabilities.name: SafetyLimitsStore (backend sync + staleness)
capabilities.behavior: `SharedPreferences("safety_limits")` with keys min_glucose, max_glucose, max_basal, max_bolus, last_fetched_ms; each getter falls back to the corresponding SafetyLimits DEFAULT_*. `updateAll(min,max,basal,bolus)` runs values through `SafetyLimits.safeOf(...)` BEFORE persisting (so even direct property reads are safe) and writes all five keys plus `System.currentTimeMillis()` in one `.commit()` (synchronous). `clear()` commits a full wipe (called on logout). `isStale(maxAgeMs = STALE_THRESHOLD_MS)` where `STALE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000L` (1 hour) returns `now - lastFetchedMs > maxAge`. `toSafetyLimits()` re-clamps via safeOf. Explicit rule in KDoc: the mobile app NEVER allows local override of safety limits — only updateAll from backend sync. `PluginRegistry.refreshSafetyLimits()` re-reads the store, pushes the new value into the shared StateFlow, and publishes SafetyLimitsChanged.
edge_cases: lastFetchedMs defaults to 0 so a never-synced install is always stale
Nothing blocks readings when limits are stale — staleness is informational at this layer

capabilities.name: CgmReading model and validation
capabilities.behavior: `data class CgmReading(glucoseMgDl: Int, trendArrow: CgmTrend, timestamp: Instant)` with `init { require(glucoseMgDl in MIN_MG_DL..MAX_MG_DL) }` where `MIN_MG_DL = 20`, `MAX_MG_DL = 500` — constructing an out-of-range reading throws IllegalArgumentException, so the type itself is a validity proof. Storage unit is mg/dL everywhere; mmol/L is display-only (÷ 18.0156, round last) and lives outside this module. `enum CgmTrend { DOUBLE_UP, SINGLE_UP, FORTY_FIVE_UP, FLAT, FORTY_FIVE_DOWN, SINGLE_DOWN, DOUBLE_DOWN, UNKNOWN }` — 8 values, no numeric mapping in the SDK; each driver maps its own wire encoding. There is no staleness field on the reading: freshness is derived from `timestamp` by consumers.
edge_cases: A throwing constructor means a parser that fails to pre-filter will crash the coroutine rather than drop the record — extract* implementations must filter before constructing
20..500 is duplicated across ~15 sites and guarded by app/src/test/.../SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest.kt; plugins/example is a documented exclusion from that guard

capabilities.name: BgmReading model and validation
capabilities.behavior: `data class BgmReading(glucoseMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant, meterName: String? = null)` with `init { require(glucoseMgDl in 20..500) }` — the bound is an inline literal here, not a reference to SafetyLimits or CgmReading constants (a known duplication site listed in the cross-repo drift doc). `meterName` is free-form and used for display/provenance (the demo sets "Demo Glucometer" and "Demo Glucometer (manual)"). No trend arrow — fingersticks are point measurements. BGM_SOURCE is multi-instance so multiple meters can be active at once and readings from different meters are distinguished only by `meterName` and the publishing `pluginId` on the event.
edge_cases: Validation is against the hardcoded 20..500, NOT against the user's narrower configured SafetyLimits — narrowing is the driver's job before construction

capabilities.name: BolusEvent model and hard 25 U cap
capabilities.behavior: `data class BolusEvent(units: Float, isAutomated: Boolean, isCorrection: Boolean, correctionUnits: Float = 0f, mealUnits: Float = 0f, source: String = "", category: String = "", timestamp: Instant)`. `init` requires each of units, correctionUnits, mealUnits to be >= 0f and <= `MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f` (hard cap: Tandem hardware max 25 U). Documented semantics: `units` is the ACTUAL delivered total from pump hardware, while correctionUnits/mealUnits are the REQUESTED breakdown, and they may not sum to `units` because (1) partial delivery from occlusion or user cancel means delivered < requested, (2) the Tandem status response (opcode 0x30) carries no breakdown so both are 0, and (3) automated boluses set mealUnits=0 regardless of the correction portion. `category` is the pump-specific string mapped through BolusCategoryProvider.
edge_cases: Two independent bolus caps exist and can disagree: the type-level 25f (units) and SafetyLimits.maxBolusDoseMilliunits (default 25_000 mU, user-narrowable). Drivers must apply the SafetyLimits one; the type cap is the backstop.
Displaying correctionUnits + mealUnits as if it equals the delivered dose would be a dosing-display bug

capabilities.name: Remaining domain models (insulin, status, history, hardware)
capabilities.behavior: `IoBReading(iob: Float, timestamp: Instant)`. `BasalReading(rate: Float, isAutomated: Boolean, activityMode: PumpActivityMode, timestamp: Instant)`. `enum PumpActivityMode { NONE, SLEEP, EXERCISE }` — documented as a pump-level feature independent of Control-IQ automation, present on all Tandem pumps; `typealias ControlIqMode = PumpActivityMode` remains as a @Deprecated backwards-compat alias. `PumpSettings(firmwareVersion, serialNumber, modelNumber: String)`. `BatteryStatus(percentage: Int, isCharging: Boolean, timestamp)`. `ReservoirReading(unitsRemaining: Float, timestamp)`. `HistoryLogRange(firstSeq: Int, lastSeq: Int)` — from HistoryLogStatusResponse opcode 59; sequences are unsigned 32-bit on the wire, stored as signed Int, documented safe because current pumps sit near ~1.3M vs Int.MAX 2_147_483_647. `HistoryLogRecord(sequenceNumber: Int, rawBytesB64: String, eventTypeId: Int, pumpTimeSeconds: Long)`. `PumpHardwareInfo(serialNumber, modelNumber, partNumber: Long, pumpRev: String, armSwVer, mspSwVer, configABits, configBBits, pcbaSn: Long, pcbaRev: String, pumpFeatures: Map<String,Boolean>)`.
edge_cases: None of these carry validation requires — only CgmReading, BgmReading and BolusEvent do
HistoryLogRecord holds raw bytes as Base64 text, so parsing is deferred to the driver's extract* methods

capabilities.name: GlucoseSource capability
capabilities.behavior: `interface GlucoseSource : PluginCapabilityInterface { fun observeReadings(): Flow<CgmReading>; suspend fun getCurrentReading(): Result<CgmReading> }`. Single-instance (GLUCOSE_SOURCE). Both shipped drivers implement observeReadings identically as a polling cold flow: `while(true) { source.getCgmReading().onSuccess { emit(it) }; delay(POLL_INTERVAL_MS) }` with `POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000L` (60 s) in both TandemGlucoseSource and MedtronicGlucoseSource. Failures are swallowed — `onSuccess` only, so a failed poll emits nothing and the loop simply waits another 60 s. Medtronic's KDoc notes the real-time stream is polling, not pump-pushed, and that cadence ownership is planned to move to the polling orchestrator in Milestone D.
edge_cases: A silently-failing poll is indistinguishable from 'no new reading' — staleness must be inferred from CgmReading.timestamp downstream
The flow never terminates; it only ends on collector cancellation

capabilities.name: InsulinSource capability
capabilities.behavior: `interface InsulinSource : PluginCapabilityInterface { suspend fun getIoB(): Result<IoBReading>; suspend fun getBasalRate(): Result<BasalReading>; suspend fun getBolusHistory(since: Instant, limits: SafetyLimits): Result<List<BolusEvent>> }`. Single-instance. `getBolusHistory` takes SafetyLimits explicitly; the documented (interface-unenforced but required) contract is that implementations REJECT — drop, not clamp — any bolus whose dose exceeds `limits.maxBolusDoseMilliunits`. Tandem's implementation forwards straight to `bleDriver.getBolusHistory(since, limits)`. Medtronic maintains a per-process `bolusCursor: Int?` guarded by a `Mutex`, seeds it on first call from a lightweight `getHistoryCursor()` read-last (returning an empty list that call), then fetches `getHistoryLogs(sinceSequence = cursor)`, advances the cursor to `records.maxOfOrNull { sequenceNumber } ?: cursor`, extracts boluses applying limits, and filters `!timestamp.isBefore(since)` as a defensive lower bound.
edge_cases: Medtronic's cursor is explicitly best-effort: it advances before persistence, so a save failure can skip a bolus on this path; the slow-loop raw-history sync (Room-persisted per sequence) is the durable, self-healing path
Cursor is not persisted across process restarts — it re-seeds past all existing history each launch

capabilities.name: PumpStatus capability and extract* safety contract
capabilities.behavior: Reads: `getBatteryStatus`, `getReservoirLevel`, `getPumpSettings`, `getPumpHardwareInfo`, `getHistoryLogs(sinceSequence: Int)`, and `getFullHistoryLogs(sinceSequence: Int)` whose DEFAULT implementation delegates to `getHistoryLogs` (full sync without lookback limits; Tandem overrides it, Medtronic does not). Three synchronous extractors take `(records, limits)`: `extractCgmFromHistoryLogs` must drop any reading outside `limits.glucoseLow..glucoseHigh` or at minimum the absolute 20-500 mg/dL range; `extractBolusesFromHistoryLogs` MUST drop (never return) events whose units exceed `limits.maxBolus`; `extractBasalFromHistoryLogs` must drop out-of-range entries. The rule everywhere is DROP, never clamp. Two lifecycle methods sit on this capability: `unpair()` (clear credentials + disconnect) and `autoReconnectIfPaired()`, both non-suspend with a TODO to become suspend once the deprecated PumpConnectionManager is removed.
edge_cases: extract* are pure functions over already-fetched records and need no live session
Medtronic derives both getPumpSettings and getPumpHardwareInfo from the same Device Information Service read (no dedicated settings characteristic)
unpair()/autoReconnectIfPaired() live on PUMP_STATUS, not DevicePlugin — a device plugin without PUMP_STATUS has no unpair path

capabilities.name: BgmSource capability
capabilities.behavior: `interface BgmSource : PluginCapabilityInterface { fun observeReadings(): Flow<BgmReading>; suspend fun getLatestReading(): Result<BgmReading> }`. Multi-instance — several meters may be active simultaneously and BGM_SOURCE never conflicts with a pump's GLUCOSE_SOURCE. Reference implementation `DemoBgmSource(simulator, safetyLimits: StateFlow<SafetyLimits>, intervalProvider: () -> Long)`: `observeReadings()` returns the simulator's cold flow started with `intervalSeconds = intervalProvider()` (evaluated once per collection, so an interval settings change only takes effect on the next collection); `getLatestReading()` returns `simulator.latestReading` or `Result.failure(IllegalStateException("No readings available yet"))`. Documented contract for authors: cold Flow, cancelled on deactivation; getLatestReading must be thread-safe; validate every reading against the CURRENT StateFlow value before emission.
edge_cases: Only one collector per ReadingSimulator instance is safe (shared mutable phase/history); the platform guarantees this via a single activation scope per plugin

capabilities.name: CalibrationTarget capability and BG validation
capabilities.behavior: `suspend fun calibrate(bgValueMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant): Result<Unit>` and `suspend fun getCalibrationStatus(): Result<CalibrationStatus>`. Single-instance. The companion provides `validateBgValue(bgValueMgDl): Result<Unit>` returning `Result.failure(IllegalArgumentException("BG calibration value $v outside safe range [20..500]"))` when `bgValueMgDl !in SafetyLimits.ABSOLUTE_MIN_GLUCOSE..SafetyLimits.ABSOLUTE_MAX_GLUCOSE`, else `Result.success(Unit)`. Division of responsibility documented in KDoc: the PLATFORM validates against absolute bounds before forwarding, so implementations need not re-check, but MAY enforce tighter device-specific limits. `CalibrationStatus(lastCalibrationTime: Instant?, isCalibrationNeeded: Boolean, nextCalibrationDue: Instant?)`. No CalibrationTarget implementation ships today (neither Tandem nor Medtronic declares it).
edge_cases: validateBgValue checks the ABSOLUTE bounds, not the user's narrowed SafetyLimits — a value inside 20..500 but outside the user's configured range still passes
Returns a Result rather than throwing, unlike the model-level requires

capabilities.name: BolusCategoryProvider capability and Tandem mapping
capabilities.behavior: `fun declaredCategories(): Set<String>` and `fun toPlatformCategory(pluginCategory: String): String?` (null for unknown). Single-instance (added in API v4 alongside `BolusEvent.category`). Purpose: pump-agnostic insulin summaries that still preserve pump-specific detail. TandemBolusCategoryProvider declares exactly {CONTROL_IQ, BG_FOOD, BG_ONLY, FOOD_ONLY, OVERRIDE, QUICK, UNKNOWN} and maps them to platform names: CONTROL_IQ->AUTO_CORRECTION, BG_FOOD->FOOD_AND_CORRECTION, BG_ONLY->CORRECTION, FOOD_ONLY->FOOD, OVERRIDE->OVERRIDE, QUICK->OTHER, UNKNOWN->OTHER. Platform names must match a `BolusCategory` enum name (that enum lives outside this module). Medtronic does not declare this capability.
edge_cases: Both QUICK and UNKNOWN collapse to OTHER — the mapping is lossy by design
Mapping is by string, so a typo yields null rather than a compile error

capabilities.name: PluginEvent hierarchy and validation
capabilities.behavior: `sealed class PluginEvent { abstract val pluginId: String }` with 8 data-class variants. Device: `NewGlucoseReading(pluginId, reading: CgmReading)`, `NewBgmReading(pluginId, reading: BgmReading)`, `InsulinDelivered(pluginId, event: BolusEvent)`, `DeviceConnected(pluginId)`, `DeviceDisconnected(pluginId)`. Calibration: `CalibrationRequested(pluginId, bgValueMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant)` whose `init` enforces `require(bgValueMgDl in 20..500)` with message "bgValueMgDl must be in 20..500, was $v" (inline literal, another drift-guard site), and `CalibrationCompleted(pluginId, success: Boolean, message: String)`. Platform-only: `SafetyLimitsChanged(pluginId, limits: SafetyLimits)`. `companion object { val PLATFORM_ONLY: Set<KClass<out PluginEvent>> = setOf(SafetyLimitsChanged::class) }` is the enforcement list.
edge_cases: CalibrationRequested is the only variant with validation; it throws rather than returning a Result
Only SafetyLimitsChanged is platform-only; any plugin can forge a NewGlucoseReading claiming another plugin's id (pluginId is unvalidated)

capabilities.name: PluginEventBus and its platform implementation
capabilities.behavior: Interface: `fun publish(event: PluginEvent)` and `fun <T : PluginEvent> subscribe(eventType: KClass<T>): Flow<T>`, plus a reified extension `inline fun <reified T> PluginEventBus.subscribe(): Flow<T>`. `PluginEventBusImpl` is a `@Singleton` over a `MutableSharedFlow<PluginEvent>(extraBufferCapacity = 256, onBufferOverflow = BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST)` — no replay, so late subscribers see nothing historical. `publish()` first checks `event::class in PluginEvent.PLATFORM_ONLY`; if so it logs a warning and RETURNS SILENTLY (no exception, no signal to the plugin). Otherwise `tryEmit`; a false result logs "Event bus buffer full, dropping event". `internal fun publishPlatform(event)` skips the platform-only check and is restricted to the `:app` module by Kotlin `internal` visibility (plugins are separate Gradle modules). `subscribe` is `events.filterIsInstance(eventType)`. Documented flow: BGM reading -> NewBgmReading -> CalibrationRequested -> CGM plugin calibrates -> CalibrationCompleted.
edge_cases: Events are droppable: a burst >256 with no fast consumer silently loses the OLDEST events — not a delivery guarantee
Blocked platform-only publishes are indistinguishable from success from the plugin's side
Kotlin `internal` is the only barrier on publishPlatform; a Swift port needs an equivalent module/access-control boundary

capabilities.name: PairingProfile / PairingStyle / PairingFault
capabilities.behavior: `enum PairingStyle { CENTRAL_SCAN, ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT }`. CENTRAL_SCAN: phone is BLE central, scans, shows a device list, user taps one (Tandem). ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT: phone is BLE peripheral, advertises, the device connects as central (Medtronic MiniMed 700-series) — no scan, no device list; the user triggers pairing from the device's own menu and picks the phone by name. `data class PairingProfile(style = CENTRAL_SCAN, advertisedName: String? = null)`; advertisedName is the exact BLE name shown on the device's pairing menu, null for central-scan. `enum PairingFault { PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED, ADVERTISE_FAILED, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, AUTH_FAILED, BOUND_ELSEWHERE }`. Rationale captured in KDoc: advertise-and-wait failures (phone can't advertise; device still bound to another phone) produce NO ConnectionState transition, so without an explicit fault the UI has nothing to show. Medtronic maps its internal MedtronicConnectionFault 1:1 (BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED -> BOUND_ELSEWHERE).
edge_cases: Central-scan plugins keep the default observePairingFault() (always null) and drive UI from ConnectionState alone
BOUND_ELSEWHERE is inferred from 'advertising with nothing connecting', i.e. a heuristic timeout, not a protocol signal

capabilities.name: Device discovery models and Tandem model detection
capabilities.behavior: `DiscoveredDevice(name: String, address: String, rssi: Int? = null, pluginId: String, metadata: Map<String,String> = emptyMap())` is the generalized discovery result; legacy `DiscoveredPump(name, address, rssi: Int)` is the Tandem-only shape the deprecated PumpScanner still uses (PumpScannerAdapter maps `rssi = device.rssi ?: 0`). `TandemPumpModel(displayName, hasScreen: Boolean?)` has TSLIM_X2("t:slim X2", hasScreen=true), MOBI("Mobi", false), UNKNOWN("Unknown Tandem Pump", null — callers should show generic instructions). `fromAdvertisedName(name: String?)`: null -> UNKNOWN; otherwise trim and collapse whitespace via `Regex("\\s+") -> " "`, then case-insensitive prefix match "tslim X2" or "t:slim X2" -> TSLIM_X2, "Tandem Mobi" -> MOBI, else UNKNOWN. It lives in the SDK because pairing UX needs model-appropriate instructions.
edge_cases: The BleScanner fallback name "Tandem Pump" deliberately resolves to UNKNOWN (asserted by test)
Empty string -> UNKNOWN
Whitespace normalization exists specifically for non-breaking/extra spaces in BLE advertisements

capabilities.name: Dashboard card descriptors and CardElement validation
capabilities.behavior: `DashboardCardDescriptor(id, title, priority: Int = 100, elements: List<CardElement>, hasDetail: Boolean = false)`; init requires id and title non-blank (whitespace-only rejected). Lower priority sorts higher; core platform cards occupy 0-50 and plugin cards should use 100+. `hasDetail=true` makes the platform render the card tappable with a chevron. `sealed class CardElement`: LargeValue(value, unit="", color=DEFAULT); Label(text, style=BODY); StatusBadge(text, color); ProgressBar(value, max, label="") requiring max and value finite, max > 0f, and value in 0f..max; IconValue(icon, value, label=""); SparkLine(values, label="") requiring values non-empty and all finite; Row(elements) and Column(elements) each requiring non-empty; Spacer(heightDp = 8) requiring heightDp >= 0. `enum UiColor { DEFAULT, SUCCESS, WARNING, ERROR, INFO, MUTED }`; `enum LabelStyle { TITLE, SUBTITLE, BODY, CAPTION }`; `enum PluginIcon { BLUETOOTH, BATTERY, RESERVOIR, INSULIN, GLUCOSE, HEART_RATE, SYNC, WARNING, CHECK, CLOCK, SETTINGS, SIGNAL, THERMOMETER }` (13).
edge_cases: An empty elements list is legal for a card; empty Row/Column/SparkLine is not
NaN/Infinity in ProgressBar or SparkLine throws — this is why the finite checks exist
Card descriptors are constructed inside a Flow, so a require() failure surfaces as a flow exception mid-render

capabilities.name: Settings descriptors and key validation
capabilities.behavior: `sealed class SettingDescriptor { abstract val key: String }` with six variants, each calling `requireValidKey(key)` in init against `VALID_KEY = Regex("^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}$")` (must start with a letter, max 128 chars total). Variants: TextInput(key, label, hint="", sensitive=false — masks input); Toggle(key, label, description=""); Slider(key, label, min, max, step=1f, unit="") additionally requiring min < max, step > 0, step <= (max - min); Dropdown(key, label, options: List<DropdownOption>) requiring options non-empty; ActionButton(key, label, style: ButtonStyle = DEFAULT); InfoText(key, text). `DropdownOption(value, label)` requires value non-blank. `enum ButtonStyle { DEFAULT, PRIMARY, DESTRUCTIVE }` (DESTRUCTIVE should get a confirmation dialog). `PluginSettingsSection(title, items)`; `PluginSettingsDescriptor(sections)` init requires all keys across all sections be distinct, error listing the duplicates.
edge_cases: Keys double as SharedPreferences keys, so the regex is also the persistence-key contract
Note the setting-key regex `{0,127}` differs from the plugin-ID regex `{1,127}` and allows `.` `-` `_` in different positions

capabilities.name: Detail screens and detail-action routing
capabilities.behavior: `DetailScreenDescriptor(title, elements: List<DetailElement>)`; init requires title non-blank, `elements.size <= MAX_ELEMENTS = 100` (explicitly to prevent UI DoS), and no duplicate keys among `DetailElement.Interactive` entries (error lists the dupes). `sealed class DetailElement { Display(element: CardElement); Interactive(setting: SettingDescriptor); SectionHeader(title) }` — SectionHeader requires non-blank title. Display elements have no keys and never collide. Empty element list is legal. Routing: `Plugin.observeDetailScreen(cardId)` returns null unless the plugin recognizes the cardId; `PluginDetailViewModel` collects it with `.flowOn(Dispatchers.IO).conflate()`, resets error on each emission, and surfaces "Plugin encountered an error loading detail content" on exception. `onAction(key)` dispatches `plugin.onDetailAction(cardId, key)` on Dispatchers.IO; failures set "Action could not be completed". Interactive setting values round-trip through the plugin's settings store.
edge_cases: Exactly 100 elements is accepted; 101 throws
observeDetailScreen is only called for cards with hasDetail=true
ViewModel skips reload when the same cardId is requested again

capabilities.name: PluginRegistry: creation, activation, mutual exclusion
capabilities.behavior: `initialize()` is one-shot (`check(initialized.compareAndSet(false,true))`). Per compile-time factory: skip if `metadata.apiVersion != PLUGIN_API_VERSION` (warn); skip if `featureGate.isEnabled(id)` is false; else validate the ID, RESERVE the id in `compileTimePluginIds` BEFORE init (so a runtime plugin cannot hijack a built-in id if init fails transiently), build the context, `factory.create()`, `plugin.initialize()`, store. Any exception -> log, drop the settings store entry, continue with the other plugins. Then discoverRuntimePlugins(), publish `_availablePlugins`, then restoreActivePlugins(). `activatePlugin(id)` under `synchronized(activationLock)`: unknown id -> failure; already active -> idempotent success; collect conflicting ids from persisted single-instance slots; call `onActivated()` FIRST (so the capability slot is never empty), then persist slots (set for single-instance, add for multi), THEN deactivate conflicts, then updateStateFlows(). `deactivatePlugin` removes from activePlugins, calls onDeactivated (exceptions logged and swallowed), clears/removes preference entries, updates flows.
edge_cases: Activation order is deliberately new-then-old so no capability slot is ever empty mid-swap; briefly two plugins hold the same single-instance capability
restoreActivePlugins clears the stored preference for a plugin whose onActivated throws
A feature-gated plugin keeps its persisted active-plugin preference untouched so re-enabling restores the user's prior selection

capabilities.name: PluginRegistry: capability slot state flows
capabilities.behavior: Exposed StateFlows: `availablePlugins: List<PluginMetadata>`, `activePumpPlugin: DevicePlugin?` = first active plugin declaring PUMP_STATUS **or** INSULIN_SOURCE, cast `as? DevicePlugin`; `activeGlucoseSource: DevicePlugin?` = first active with GLUCOSE_SOURCE; `activeCalibrationTarget: DevicePlugin?` = first active with CALIBRATION_TARGET; `activeBgmSources: Set<DevicePlugin>` = all active with BGM_SOURCE filtered to DevicePlugin; `activeDataSyncPlugins: Set<Plugin>` = all active with DATA_SYNC (Plugin, not DevicePlugin); `allActivePlugins: List<Plugin>`; `runtimePlugins: List<RuntimePluginInfo(metadata, jarFileName, isActive)>`. `refreshSafetyLimits()` re-reads SafetyLimitsStore, writes the shared `_safetyLimits` StateFlow, and publishes `SafetyLimitsChanged(pluginId = PLATFORM_PLUGIN_ID = "platform")` via publishPlatform.
edge_cases: A non-DevicePlugin declaring GLUCOSE_SOURCE (e.g. the Nightscout source plugin) is silently excluded from these DevicePlugin-typed slots by the `as? DevicePlugin` cast
activePumpPlugin uses firstOrNull over a ConcurrentHashMap's values — iteration order is unspecified if two plugins somehow match

capabilities.name: Runtime plugin loading (DEX JAR sideloading)
capabilities.behavior: `DexPluginLoader.discover()` lists `*.jar` in `filesDir/plugins`, creating `codeCacheDir/plugin_dex` as the DEX output dir. `loadJar` builds a `DexClassLoader(jarPath, dexOut, null, context.classLoader)`, reads `META-INF/plugin.json` bounded to `MAX_MANIFEST_SIZE = 65_536` chars (a manifest with anything past the limit is rejected), parses it, then rejects the JAR if `manifest.apiVersion != PLUGIN_API_VERSION` or if the id fails `VALID_PLUGIN_ID = Regex("^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,127}$")`. It then `loadClass(manifest.factoryClass)`, `getConstructor().newInstance()`, and casts to PluginFactory (null cast -> rejected). Any exception yields null and the other JARs still load. `PluginManifest.parse` requires non-blank factoryClass, id, name, version, an integer apiVersion >= 1; author and description default to "". Registry install/discovery additionally rejects ids colliding with `compileTimePluginIds` or already-loaded plugins, deleting the JAR on failure.
edge_cases: Known limitation documented: plugins load in-process with the app classloader as parent, so they can reflect over host classes; full process isolation was deliberately NOT done because it 'adds significant complexity', relying instead on the trust model (explicit user install with a security warning)
apiVersion=1 manifests (including the shipped example) are rejected against the current version 5

capabilities.name: Plugin JAR file management
capabilities.behavior: `PluginFileManager.installPlugin(uri)`: ensure `filesDir/plugins` exists; derive filename from the URI's last path segment (fallback `plugin_<epochMillis>.jar`); REQUIRE a `.jar` suffix (case-insensitive) else fail; sanitize with `Regex("[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]") -> "_"`; canonical-path check that the destination starts with `pluginsDir.canonicalPath + File.separator` (path-traversal guard, `SecurityException` otherwise); fail if the file already exists; stream-copy while counting bytes and abort+delete past `MAX_PLUGIN_SIZE_BYTES = 50 MB` (50L*1024*1024); verify the first 4 bytes equal ZIP magic `PK\x03\x04` (0x50 0x4B 0x03 0x04) else delete and fail; finally `setReadOnly()` because Android's DexClassLoader rejects writable DEX files. `removePlugin` re-runs the canonical prefix check (with the trailing separator, to defeat `plugins_evil/` prefix collisions), calls `setWritable(true)`, then deletes. `listInstalledJars()` filters by extension.
edge_cases: Sanitization can map two distinct source names onto one destination, which then trips the already-exists check
A truncated/invalid archive is deleted only after being fully written to disk

capabilities.name: Runtime plugin sandbox (RestrictedContext)
capabilities.behavior: `RestrictedContext : ContextWrapper` throws `SecurityException("Runtime plugins cannot call <op>")` for: getBaseContext, startActivity(×2), startActivities(×2), startService, startForegroundService, stopService, bindService, getContentResolver, sendBroadcast(×2), sendOrderedBroadcast(×3), registerReceiver(×4 overloads), getSharedPreferences, openFileOutput, openFileInput, deleteFile, getDir, getDatabasePath, openOrCreateDatabase(×2), deleteDatabase, createDeviceProtectedStorageContext, createPackageContext. `getApplicationContext()` returns `this` (trapped). `getSystemService(name)` is allowlisted to exactly {BLUETOOTH_SERVICE, LOCATION_SERVICE, POWER_SERVICE, ALARM_SERVICE, SENSOR_SERVICE, USB_SERVICE, WIFI_SERVICE}; everything else throws. WINDOW_SERVICE is deliberately excluded with the stated reason that WindowManager can add overlay views when SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is held. filesDir/cacheDir/packageName remain available. Stated design philosophy: safety enforcement comes from SafetyLimits synced from the backend, not from blanket Context restrictions, because drivers genuinely need hardware access.
edge_cases: ScopedCredentialProvider deliberately uses the UNrestricted base context for its own SharedPreferences (the restricted wrapper blocks getSharedPreferences)
Compile-time plugins (Tandem, Medtronic) receive the full unrestricted context

capabilities.name: Plugin feature gate (kill switch)
capabilities.behavior: `fun interface PluginFeatureGate { fun isEnabled(pluginId: String): Boolean }`, checked in PluginRegistry.initialize BEFORE the plugin is created. A gated-off plugin is never instantiated, so it is absent from Available Plugins, has no pairing entry, and is never polled — fully invisible and inert. `BuildConfigPluginFeatureGate` is default-on: `when (pluginId) { MedtronicDevicePlugin.PLUGIN_ID -> BuildConfig.MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED; else -> true }`. Documented as the mobile analogue of the backend's per-integration kill switches (e.g. MEDTRONIC_CONNECT_ENABLED); the Medtronic read-only BLE driver ships BETA behind it (default true, build with MEDTRONIC_DRIVER_ENABLED=false to ship it off). The gate references the driver's canonical PLUGIN_ID constant directly so the switch can never silently drift onto a nonexistent id (which would leave it always enabled).
edge_cases: Gating a plugin off intentionally leaves its persisted active-plugin preference intact so re-enabling restores the prior selection

capabilities.name: Deprecated pump interfaces and their registry adapters
capabilities.behavior: Four @Deprecated interfaces remain in the SDK, all pointing at DevicePlugin/PumpStatus: `PumpDriver` (connect/disconnect/getIoB/getBasalRate/getBolusHistory(since, limits = SafetyLimits())/getPumpSettings/getBatteryStatus/getReservoirLevel/getCgmStatus/getHistoryLogs/getFullHistoryLogs(default-delegating)/getPumpHardwareInfo/observeConnectionState — explicitly documented as having NO delivery/control methods, strictly read-only); `PumpConnectionManager` (connectionState, pairingProfile, pairingFault StateFlows + connect(address, pairingCode?)/disconnect/unpair/autoReconnectIfPaired); `PumpScanner` (scan(): Flow<DiscoveredPump>); `HistoryLogParser` (the three extract* methods with `limits: SafetyLimits = SafetyLimits()` defaults). `:app` binds each to an adapter over PluginRegistry: PumpDriverAdapter (routes CGM to activeGlucoseSource, everything else to activePumpPlugin, returns `NoActivePluginException` failure when absent, rethrows CancellationException), PumpConnectionAdapter (flatMapLatest/stateIn on Dispatchers.Main.immediate, wraps pairingCode into `config["pairingCode"]`), PumpScannerAdapter (`rssi ?: 0`), HistoryLogParserAdapter (empty list when no active plugin).
edge_cases: HistoryLogParserAdapter returns an EMPTY list when no pump plugin is active — indistinguishable from 'no records', which could mask data loss
The deprecated defaults (`SafetyLimits()`) silently substitute absolute limits when a caller omits the user's configured limits

capabilities.name: Read-only capability set (deliberate non-feature)
capabilities.behavior: Explicit documented decision: the capability enum is intentionally limited to data collection and device management. The SDK exposes NO insulin delivery primitives — no bolus dosing, no basal rate changes, no therapeutic write surface — and the docs state AI workflows have no architectural path to such a surface. The device-management commands that do exist (`CalibrationTarget.calibrate()`, `PumpStatus.unpair()`, `PumpStatus.autoReconnectIfPaired()`, `DevicePlugin.connect()/disconnect()`) are classified as session/lifecycle operations, not therapy. PumpDriver's KDoc repeats this: 'This interface intentionally has NO methods for insulin delivery, pump setting changes, or any control operations.' Both shipped drivers restate READ-ONLY in file headers. Recorded follow-up (defense-in-depth, not yet built): capability enforcement at the plugin registry boundary, where the platform would refuse to load plugins declaring capabilities outside the official enum — tracked in the platform repo ROADMAP §Phase 1.
edge_cases: Today the only barrier against a plugin declaring an unknown capability is that PluginCapability is a closed Kotlin enum — a Swift port must keep the capability type closed

capabilities.name: DemoGlucometerPlugin (reference driver)
capabilities.behavior: Non-device `Plugin` (not DevicePlugin) with id `com.example.glycemicgpt.demo-glucometer`, name "Demo Glucometer", version 1.0.0, apiVersion = PLUGIN_API_VERSION, declaring {BGM_SOURCE, DATA_SYNC} — both multi-instance, chosen explicitly so it never conflicts with a real pump's GLUCOSE_SOURCE. initialize() stores the context and builds `DemoBgmSource(simulator, ctx.safetyLimits, intervalProvider = { settingsStore.getFloat("sim_interval", 30f).toLong() })`. onActivated() returns early if `sim_enabled` (default true) is false; otherwise creates `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default + SupervisorJob())`, launches the simulator flow, and per reading increments readingCount, sets lastSyncTime, publishes `PluginEvent.NewBgmReading`, and decays `simulatedBattery` by 0.1 from a start of 87f (floor 0). onDeactivated cancels the scope; shutdown cancels the scope and nulls context/bgmSource. getCapability returns bgmSource for BgmSource::class only — DATA_SYNC deliberately returns nothing since no interface exists.
edge_cases: Uses println() rather than a logger
Changing sim_interval mid-run has no effect until reactivation (the interval is read once when the flow starts)
onActivated with simulation disabled leaves isActive=false, so the sync card shows 'Disconnected'

capabilities.name: DemoGlucometerPlugin UI surfaces
capabilities.behavior: observeDashboardCards() is an infinite `flow { ...; emit(cards); delay(5000L) }` (5 s repaint) emitting two cards. Card `demo-glucometer-status` (priority 100, hasDetail=true): LargeValue of the latest glucose or "--" colored MUTED when null, ERROR when < 70, WARNING when > 180, else SUCCESS; StatusBadge "Simulated"/INFO; a Row of IconValue BATTERY "<int>%" and GLUCOSE "<count>"; a SparkLine of history when non-empty; a ProgressBar(value=simulatedBattery, max=100f). Card `demo-glucometer-sync` (priority 110): Label with "Last sync: HH:mm:ss" (system zone) or "No data synced yet", IconValue SYNC with the record count, StatusBadge Connected/SUCCESS vs Disconnected/MUTED. Settings: three sections — Simulation Settings (Toggle sim_enabled, Slider sim_interval 5..300 step 5 sec, Dropdown glucose_unit mg_dl/mmol_l), Data Sync (TextInput sync_url, Toggle auto_sync, ActionButton sync_now PRIMARY, ActionButton clear_data DESTRUCTIVE), About (InfoText about_info, InfoText safety_info showing the live min-max limits).
edge_cases: The 70/180 color thresholds are hardcoded in the demo, unrelated to SafetyLimits
safety_info falls back to a generic string when context is null (post-shutdown)
glucose_unit and sync_url/auto_sync/sync_now/clear_data are declared but never acted on — pure UI demonstration

capabilities.name: DemoGlucometerPlugin detail screen + manual entry
capabilities.behavior: observeDetailScreen returns null unless `cardId == "demo-glucometer-status"`, otherwise an infinite flow emitting a rebuilt DetailScreenDescriptor every 3000 ms. Layout: SectionHeader "Recent Readings" then either a CAPTION placeholder or the last 10 timestamped readings reversed as "HH:mm:ss  -  <int> mg/dL"; a SparkLine when history size >= 2; SectionHeader "Manual Entry" with TextInput `detail_bg_value` (hint "Enter value between 20-500") and ActionButton `detail_record_reading` (PRIMARY); SectionHeader "Simulator Controls" repeating the sim_enabled Toggle and sim_interval Slider; SectionHeader "Safety Info" with the limits text. onDetailAction for `detail_record_reading` reads `detail_bg_value` from the settings store, parses with toIntOrNull, and accepts only `value in 20..500`: it calls simulator.addManualReading, increments the count, sets lastSyncTime, publishes NewBgmReading with meterName "Demo Glucometer (manual)", then clears the input field. Invalid input only prints a message.
edge_cases: The manual-entry bound is the hardcoded 20..500, not the user's configured SafetyLimits — a manual reading outside the narrowed range still gets published
Invalid input gives the user no UI feedback

capabilities.name: ReadingSimulator (synthetic BGM generator)
capabilities.behavior: `start(intervalSeconds: Long, safetyLimits: StateFlow<SafetyLimits>): Flow<BgmReading>` — a cold flow that `require(intervalSeconds > 0)`, then loops while the coroutine is active: generate a raw value, read `safetyLimits.value` FRESH each iteration (so backend limit changes take effect immediately — the behavior real drivers must copy), drop the value with a printed message if `raw < min || raw > max`, else construct `BgmReading(raw, Instant.now(), "Demo Glucometer")`, set latestReading, record history, emit; then `delay(intervalSeconds * 1000L)`. `generateRawValue()`: `base = 130.0 + 50.0 * sin(phase)` (range 80-180), `jitter = rng.nextDouble(-10.0, 10.0)`, `phase += 2π/12` (a full cycle every 12 readings), returns `(base + jitter).roundToInt().coerceIn(20, 500)`. `addManualReading(Float)` requires 20f..500f then records history. History is two synchronized lists (`List<Float>` for sparkline, `List<Pair<Instant,Float>>` for the detail screen), each trimmed from the front to `MAX_HISTORY = 12`.
edge_cases: The delay happens even when a reading is dropped, so the cadence is unaffected by filtering
Note the asymmetry: generateRawValue CLAMPS to 20..500 while the SafetyLimits check DROPS — clamping here is safe only because 80-180±10 never approaches the bounds
Only one collector per instance is safe (shared phase/history); the platform enforces this via a single activation scope

capabilities.name: Fidelity of the example driver as a reference
capabilities.behavior: What it faithfully demonstrates: the full lifecycle (initialize/onActivated/onDeactivated/shutdown with correct resource ownership), reactive safety-limit reads on every iteration, drop-not-clamp filtering, event-bus publication with the plugin's own id, every SettingDescriptor and CardElement variant, detail screens with interactive elements and action routing, per-plugin settings persistence, and the runtime-plugin packaging path (no-arg factory + META-INF/plugin.json + d8 DEX conversion). What it does NOT demonstrate: it is a plain `Plugin`, not a `DevicePlugin` — no connect/disconnect/scan, no ConnectionState, no pairing profile or fault, no credential provider use, no BLE, no DebugLogger use, no CalibrationTarget/CalibrationRequested participation, and no getCapability entry for its declared DATA_SYNC capability. Its manifest apiVersion is 1 while the platform requires 5, so as shipped it would be rejected by DexPluginLoader.
edge_cases: README's manifest table also says apiVersion must be `1`, matching neither the code (5) nor the architecture doc (2)

capabilities.name: Build configuration and toolchain pins
capabilities.behavior: `:pump-driver-api` is an Android library: `compileSdk = 35`, `minSdk = 30`, Java source/target 17, `kotlinOptions.jvmTarget = "17"`, namespace `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.pump.api`, `consumerProguardFiles("consumer-rules.pro")`. Its only production dependency is `api(libs.coroutines.core)` — kotlinx-coroutines-core 1.10.2 per the Gradle lockfile — plus junit 4.13.2 for tests; Kotlin stdlib/compiler 2.1.0. Notably it has NO Android framework dependency in code except `android.content.Context` in PluginContext. consumer-rules.pro is intentionally empty of keep rules (module classes are accessed programmatically, not via reflective serialization), but `:app`'s proguard keeps `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.domain.plugin.**`, `domain.pump.**` and `domain.model.**` for capability reflection. The example plugin is a standalone JVM project: `kotlin("jvm") version "2.0.21"`, JVM 17, `compileOnly(files("libs/pump-driver-api.jar"))` and `compileOnly("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.10.2")`, jar base name `example-plugin`.
edge_cases: Runtime plugin packaging requires `d8 --output dex-out/ build/libs/example-plugin.jar` then `jar uf example-plugin.jar -C dex-out classes.dex` — DEX bytecode plus the original manifest in one archive

safety_critical: Glucose validity bounds 20..500 mg/dL are the load-bearing invariant and are duplicated across ~15 sites (SafetyLimits.DEFAULT_/ABSOLUTE_MIN|MAX_GLUCOSE, CgmReading.MIN_MG_DL/MAX_MG_DL, BgmReading require, PluginEvent.CalibrationRequested require, CalibrationTarget.validateBgValue, plus app/wear sites). A drift-guard unit test (app/src/test/.../contract/SafetyConstantDriftGuardTest.kt) enumerates them; docs/contract/safety-constants.md is the source of truth. A Swift port must either consolidate to one constant or reproduce an equivalent guard.

CgmReading, BgmReading and BolusEvent validate in their constructors and THROW. A driver that constructs one from unfiltered pump data crashes the coroutine instead of dropping a record. Swift value types must decide deliberately between throwing initializers and failable ones — and any change to failable silently converts crashes into dropped data.

DROP, never CLAMP. All three PumpStatus.extract* methods and InsulinSource.getBolusHistory must discard out-of-range readings/doses rather than coerce them. A clamped 900 mg/dL becoming 500, or a clamped 40 U bolus becoming 25 U, would display fabricated clinical data.

Two independent bolus caps must both be honored: BolusEvent.MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f (type-level, units) and SafetyLimits.maxBolusDoseMilliunits (default/absolute 25_000 mU, user-narrowable). The milliunits-vs-units ×1000 scale difference between SafetyLimits and the reading models is an easy conversion bug with dosing-display consequences.

SafetyLimits.safeOf() clamps rather than throws for backend input, and its ordering (min clamped to 20..499 first, max then coerced to clampedMin+1..500) means a nonsensical config like (min=450, max=300) silently yields a 1 mg/dL-wide accept window (450..451) with no warning — nearly all readings would then be dropped.

SafetyLimits must be read from the StateFlow's CURRENT value on every validation pass, not cached at initialize(). ReadingSimulator documents this explicitly; caching would let a driver keep validating against revoked, wider limits after a backend narrowing.

The PluginEventBus is lossy by design: MutableSharedFlow(extraBufferCapacity = 256, onBufferOverflow = DROP_OLDEST), no replay. It is NOT a delivery guarantee — NewGlucoseReading / NewBgmReading / CalibrationRequested can be silently dropped under burst, and blocked platform-only publishes return silently. Any alerting built on it needs its own guarantee.

Glucose polling is fixed at 60_000 ms in both shipped GlucoseSource implementations, and failed polls are swallowed via `onSuccess` only — a persistently failing pump produces an indefinitely stale display with no distinguishing signal. Staleness must be derived from CgmReading.timestamp; nothing in the API surfaces it.

CalibrationTarget.validateBgValue checks ABSOLUTE bounds (20..500), not the user's narrowed SafetyLimits, and the demo's manual-entry path also uses the raw 20..500 literal. Sending an out-of-user-range fingerstick as a CGM calibration is a direct patient-safety path.

Medtronic's bolus cursor advances on a successful fetch BEFORE the orchestrator persists, so a transient save failure can skip a bolus on that path. This is explicitly tolerated only because the slow-loop raw-history sync (Room-persisted per sequence, restored on restart) is the durable path. Porting the fast path without the durable path would lose insulin records.
HistoryLogParserAdapter returns an EMPTY list when no pump plugin is active, which is indistinguishable from 'no new records' — silent data loss rather than an error.
DebugLogger carries raw glucose/insulin/device-identifier bytes; implementations must retain cargoHex/parsedValue only in debug builds and never persist them unencrypted.

Runtime plugins get UNencrypted credential storage (ScopedCredentialProvider) and load in-process with the app's classloader as parent — both accepted risks under the stated trust model, with documented revisit triggers.

Activation deliberately calls onActivated() on the new plugin BEFORE deactivating the conflicting one, so two plugins transiently hold the same single-instance capability (e.g. two live GLUCOSE_SOURCEs). The window is intentional (slot never empty) but readings from both can arrive.
The read-only capability model is the top-level safety architecture: no bolus/basal/therapeutic write surface exists anywhere in the SDK. Any port must preserve this closed capability set.

Coverage is complete for the stated scope at uniform depth: every file in plugins/pump-driver-api (23 main sources + 5 test sources + build files) and every file in plugins/example was read in full, plus the platform-side files the API's contracts depend on (PluginRegistry, PluginEventBusImpl, PluginSettingsStoreImpl, PluginPreferences, PluginFeatureGate, RestrictedPluginContext, DexPluginLoader, PluginManifest, PluginFileManager, SafetyLimitsStore, the four legacy adapters, PluginModule, PluginDetailViewModel), docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md and docs/contract/safety-constants.md. The shipped Tandem/Medtronic plugin+capability classes were read only as far as they show how the interfaces are implemented (poll intervals, lifecycle mapping, extract* delegation); their BLE stacks (auth, protocol, parsers, connection managers, reconnect/backoff) are a separate subsystem and are NOT covered here.

Three doc/code inconsistencies a porter must resolve rather than copy: (1) PLUGIN_API_VERSION is 5 in code, "2" in docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md (two places), and "1" in plugins/example/README.md and META-INF/plugin.json — the shipped example JAR would be rejected by DexPluginLoader's exact-match check today. (2) docs say androidContext "exposes the full application Context ... must be replaced with a restricted interface before any runtime-loaded plugin support is introduced", but RestrictedPluginContext already exists and is used — the PluginContext KDoc is the accurate one. (3) PumpStatus KDoc references `SafetyLimits.glucoseLow`/`glucoseHigh` and `maxBolus`, which are not the actual property names (minGlucoseMgDl/maxGlucoseMgDl/maxBolusDoseMilliunits).

Two structural facts worth carrying into Swift: capability lookup is KClass-keyed with unchecked casts, which needs a protocol-witness or type-keyed registry instead; and `internal` Kotlin visibility is the ONLY thing preventing plugins from calling publishPlatform (the platform-only event bypass), so the port needs a real module/access boundary there.
