port.subsystem: Pump driver API and safety model (`:pump-driver-api` SDK + `plugins/example` reference driver + the `:app`-side enforcement the API contracts depend on: PluginRegistry, PluginEventBusImpl, RestrictedPluginContext, DexPluginLoader, PluginFileManager, SafetyLimitsStore, legacy adapters) — ported to a Swift `PumpDriverAPI` SPM package plus compile-time-linked driver targets for iOS 17+/watchOS 10+.

ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Swift `protocol Plugin` with `metadata`, `capabilities`, `initialize(_:)`, `shutdown()`, `onActivated()`, `onDeactivated()`, `settingsDescriptor()`, `dashboardCards: AsyncStream<[DashboardCardDescriptor]>`, `capability<T>(_:)`. The two defaulted members become protocol-extension defaults (`detailScreen(cardId:)` = nil, `onDetailAction(cardId:actionKey:)` = no-op). Lifecycle methods are `@MainActor` to reproduce Kotlin's main-thread serialization; capability methods stay non-isolated `async`. Throwing semantics map to `throws` on initialize/onActivated (registry catches, skips the driver, drops its settings entry) and `try?` on onDeactivated/shutdown (logged, continue).

`enum PluginCapability: CaseIterable` with the same 7 cases and two static `Set` members (5 single-instance, 2 multi-instance). Swift has no enum-companion `init`, so the class-load exhaustiveness guard becomes an XCTest asserting `Set(allCases) == singleInstance.union(multiInstance)` and that the two sets are disjoint, run in a required CI job. Keeping the enum closed — no raw-string construction, no `@unknown default` escape — is what preserves the read-only architectural guarantee.

Replace KClass dispatch and unchecked casts with `func capability<T: PluginCapabilityInterface>(_ type: T.Type) -> T?`, backed by an `[ObjectIdentifier: any PluginCapabilityInterface]` map built during `initialize()` or a `switch` on `T.self`. The six `as*()` extensions become protocol-extension computed properties (`var glucoseSource: (any GlucoseSource)?`). Strictly safer than Kotlin — no `@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")`. Declaring a capability and returning nil for it still works, preserving the demo driver's DATA_SYNC behavior.

`final class PluginContext` carrying `pluginId`, `settingsStore`, `credentialProvider`, `debugLogger`, `eventBus`, `apiVersion`, `safetyLimits`. The `androidContext` field is deleted outright — iOS has no per-app Context object and drivers reach CoreBluetooth directly. `StateFlow<SafetyLimits>` becomes a shared `SafetyLimitsPublisher` exposing `.value` (for the mandatory read-on-every-validation-pass) plus an `AsyncStream` for observers. One instance shared by all drivers, mutated only by the registry, exactly as today.

`UserDefaults(suiteName: "plugin_settings_<pluginId>")` reproduces per-plugin namespacing, survival across deactivation and app update, and wipe on uninstall; removal of a driver's whole store maps to `removePersistentDomain(forName:)`. Same four typed getter/setter pairs with defaults plus `remove`. One behavior delta to record: reading a key with the wrong typed accessor returns the zero value rather than throwing ClassCastException, so type confusion becomes silent — mitigate with a per-driver key-to-type table asserted in tests.

Keychain `kSecClassGenericPassword`, service `plugin_creds_<sanitizedId>`, accounts `paired_address`, `pairing_code`, `jpake_derived_secret`, `jpake_server_nonce`, accessibility `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` (required for background BLE reconnect after reboot; ThisDeviceOnly keeps secrets out of iCloud and encrypted backups). Same 9-method surface; `isPaired()` = item exists for `paired_address`. Two deltas: Keychain items survive app deletion, so a first-launch sentinel must purge orphans; and every driver now gets real encrypted storage, closing the Android runtime-plugin plaintext gap by construction.

Same protocol, `enum Direction { case tx, rx }`, same `logPacket` and `updateLastPacket` signatures with Swift default arguments. `toSpacedHex` is a one-line map over `Data` producing the identical lowercase space-separated string. Enforce the KDoc security clause harder than Android: the implementation retaining `cargoHex`/`parsedValue` compiles only under `#if DEBUG` into an in-memory ring buffer; the release implementation records opcode, txId, size and error only. Never route payloads through OSLog (sysdiagnose capture); any persisted file needs `.completeUnlessOpen` Data Protection.

ports_cleanly.capability: SafetyLimits value type and hard bounds
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `struct SafetyLimits: Equatable` with the same four Int fields and defaults and an `init(...) throws` reproducing all five checks as typed errors — `throws`, not `precondition`, which would trap the whole process. Same DEFAULT_* and ABSOLUTE_* statics (today identical values). Milliunits stay `Int`, preserving the x1000 scale discipline against the Float-unit reading models. The boundary tests (19, -1, 501, min==max, basal 0/15001, bolus 0/25001) port one-for-one to XCTest.

`static func safeOf(...) -> SafetyLimits` clamping in exactly the Android order: min into 20...499 first, then max into (clampedMin+1)...500, then basal 1...15000, bolus 1...25000. `coerceIn` maps to a `ClosedRange.clamping` helper. The (min 450, max 300) -> (450, 451) and (bolus 0) -> 1 cases become ported assertions. Add the one thing Android lacks: emit a structured log and telemetry event whenever any input was clamped, so a nonsensical backend config is observable instead of silent.

`UserDefaults` suite `safety_limits` (or the App Group suite, since the watch and widget also render limit-dependent state) with the same five keys and DEFAULT_* fallbacks. `updateAll` runs values through `safeOf` before persisting; UserDefaults writes hit the in-memory domain synchronously so `.commit()` semantics hold. `clear()` maps to `removePersistentDomain`. `isStale(maxAge: TimeInterval = 3600)` over `Date`. Registry refresh republishes into the shared publisher and emits `SafetyLimitsChanged(pluginId: "platform")`. A never-synced install stays stale (lastFetched 0).

`struct CgmReading { glucoseMgDl: Int; trend: CgmTrend; timestamp: Date }` with a throwing init enforcing 20...500 — throwing rather than failable keeps the Android contract that unfiltered data is a defect, and forces a `try` at every construction site. 8-case `CgmTrend` with no raw values and per-driver wire mapping, as today. `Date` replaces `Instant`; the seconds-Double vs nanosecond-Long precision difference is irrelevant at 5-minute CGM cadence, but ISO-8601 must be pinned for backend round-trips. mg/dL stays the storage unit; mmol/L remains display-only.

`struct BgmReading { glucoseMgDl: Int; timestamp: Date; meterName: String? }` with the same throwing 20...500 init and no trend arrow. Multi-instance semantics unchanged: several meters active at once, distinguished only by `meterName` and the publishing `pluginId` on the event. Port the Android inline literal to a reference to the single consolidated `GlucoseBounds.absolute` constant rather than creating a second Swift duplication site. Narrowing to the user's configured limits stays the driver's job before construction.

ports_cleanly.capability: BolusEvent model and hard 25 U cap
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `struct BolusEvent` with the same 8 fields; `units`, `correctionUnits`, `mealUnits` stay `Float` (32-bit, matching Kotlin) so dose display rounds identically to Android and the backend. Throwing init enforcing 0...25 on each. Keep both caps distinct: `BolusEvent.maxBolusUnits: Float = 25` as the type backstop, `SafetyLimits.maxBolusDoseMilliunits: Int` as the user-narrowable filter drivers must apply. Preserve the documented semantic that `units` is delivered total while correction/meal are the requested breakdown and need not sum.

ports_cleanly.capability: Remaining domain models (insulin, status, history, hardware)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Mechanical struct translation of IoBReading, BasalReading, PumpSettings, BatteryStatus, ReservoirReading, HistoryLogRange, HistoryLogRecord and PumpHardwareInfo, plus 3-case `PumpActivityMode` with a deprecated `ControlIqMode` typealias. `Long` becomes `Int64`; HistoryLogRange sequences become `Int`, 64-bit on every iOS device, which eliminates the Android unsigned-32-in-signed-Int concern entirely. Keep `rawBytesB64` as a Base64 `String` at the model boundary for serialization parity, decoding to `Data` only inside driver parsers. None of these carry validation, as today.

`protocol InsulinSource` with `getIoB() async -> Result<IoBReading>`, `getBasalRate() async -> Result<BasalReading>`, `getBolusHistory(since: Date, limits: SafetyLimits) async -> Result<[BolusEvent]>`. Passing limits explicitly rather than caching them carries over unchanged, as does the drop-never-clamp rejection of doses above `maxBolusDoseMilliunits`. Medtronic's Mutex-guarded `bolusCursor` becomes an `actor`, its lazy seed-from-getHistoryCursor first call, cursor advance to max sequence, and defensive `timestamp >= since` filter all preserved. Cursor persistence is addressed under risks.

`protocol BgmSource` with `readings: AsyncStream<BgmReading>` (cold — a fresh stream per call, terminated by consuming-Task cancellation) and `getLatestReading() async -> Result<BgmReading>` returning the same failure when nothing has been read yet. The `intervalProvider` closure ports verbatim, preserving the documented 'interval change takes effect only on next collection' behavior. Multi-instance registration is unchanged and never conflicts with a pump's GLUCOSE_SOURCE. Thread-safety of `getLatestReading` is satisfied by making the reference implementation an `actor`.

`protocol CalibrationTarget` with `calibrate(bgValueMgDl:timestamp:) async -> Result<Void>` and `getCalibrationStatus() async -> Result<CalibrationStatus>`, plus a static `validateBgValue(_:) -> Result<Void>` returning the same failure text for values outside the absolute 20...500. The documented division stands: the platform validates against absolute bounds before forwarding; implementations may enforce tighter device limits. `CalibrationStatus` is a 3-field struct with optional Dates. No shipped implementation today — port the contract and its tests, not an implementation.

`protocol BolusCategoryProvider` with `declaredCategories() -> Set<String>` and a mapping function. Swift lets this be strengthened for free: return `BolusCategory?` (the platform enum) instead of `String?`, converting Android's 'a typo yields nil at runtime' into a compile error while keeping the deliberately lossy QUICK->OTHER and UNKNOWN->OTHER collapse. Tandem's 7 declared categories and their 7 platform mappings port verbatim; Medtronic still does not declare the capability.

Swift `enum PluginEvent` with 8 associated-value cases and a `pluginId` computed property — a sealed class maps more naturally to an enum than to a class hierarchy. `CalibrationRequested`'s 20...500 requirement becomes a throwing static factory, since enum cases cannot throw. Platform-only enforcement becomes stronger than Kotlin's runtime set membership: give the `SafetyLimitsChanged` payload a `package`-access initializer so a driver in a separate target cannot construct the case at all, rather than having its publish silently swallowed.

`protocol PluginEventBus { func publish(_:); func subscribe<T>(_ type: T.Type) -> AsyncStream<T> }`. Implementation is an actor holding per-subscriber `AsyncStream.Continuation`s created with `bufferingPolicy: .bufferingNewest(256)` — exactly reproducing 256-slot DROP_OLDEST with no replay, and improving on Kotlin by confining a slow consumer's drops to that consumer. `publishPlatform` lives only in the app module and constructs platform-only cases via the `package`-access initializer, so a separate driver target is a genuine access boundary rather than Kotlin's `internal`.

ports_cleanly.capability: Dashboard card descriptors and CardElement validation
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `struct DashboardCardDescriptor` with a throwing init (non-blank id and title, whitespace-only rejected) and `indirect enum CardElement` with the same 9 cases behind throwing factories carrying the same finite/non-empty/range checks. UiColor (6), LabelStyle (4) and PluginIcon (13) become plain enums mapped to a SwiftUI style catalog and SF Symbols. Priority ordering (0-50 core, 100+ plugin, lower sorts higher) and `hasDetail` chevron behavior are unchanged. Empty `elements` stays legal; empty Row/Column/SparkLine still throws.

`enum SettingDescriptor` with the same 6 cases, each built through a throwing factory applying `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}$` — keys remain both UI identifiers and persistence keys. Slider's min<max, step>0, step<=(max-min) and Dropdown's non-empty options and non-blank values port as-is. `PluginSettingsDescriptor` still rejects duplicate keys across sections and lists the duplicates. `ButtonStyle.destructive` drives a SwiftUI `.confirmationDialog`. The renderer auto-persists Toggle/Slider/Dropdown/TextInput and writes a timestamp for ActionButton taps.

`DetailScreenDescriptor` with a throwing init: non-blank title, at most 100 elements (100 accepted, 101 rejected — the explicit UI-DoS guard), and no duplicate keys among Interactive elements. `enum DetailElement { display, interactive, sectionHeader }` with non-blank section titles; Display elements have no keys and never collide; empty element lists stay legal. The ViewModel becomes an `@Observable` object consuming the stream off the main actor with latest-wins conflation, resetting error per emission and surfacing the same two user-facing strings. Actions dispatch off-main; detail is only requested for `hasDetail` cards; same-cardId reload is still skipped.

A `@MainActor final class DriverRegistry` with one-shot initialization. Per driver: apiVersion check, feature-gate check, ID regex validation, reserve the id in `compileTimeIds` before init so a later registration cannot hijack it, build context, create, initialize, store; any throw logs, drops the settings entry, and continues with the remaining drivers. Activation preserves the exact order — `onActivated()` on the new driver first, then persist capability slots, then deactivate conflicts, then republish — so a single-instance slot is never empty mid-swap. MainActor isolation replaces `synchronized(activationLock)`; a reentrant actor must not be used here.

Eight `@Observable` properties (or AsyncStreams) with identical selection rules: activePumpPlugin = first active declaring PUMP_STATUS or INSULIN_SOURCE cast to DevicePlugin; activeGlucoseSource; activeCalibrationTarget; activeBgmSources as a Set; activeDataSyncPlugins typed `any Plugin` rather than DevicePlugin; allActivePlugins; availablePlugins. `as? DevicePlugin` becomes `as? any DevicePlugin`, preserving the silent exclusion of non-device sources such as a Nightscout-backed glucose source. Replace the ConcurrentHashMap `firstOrNull` with an order-stable array so the unspecified-iteration-order ambiguity disappears.

`protocol PluginFeatureGate { func isEnabled(_ pluginId: String) -> Bool }`, evaluated before instantiation so a gated driver is never created, never listed, never paired and never polled — identical semantics. Backed by an `.xcconfig` build setting surfaced as a generated Swift constant, which the fork-and-build model already requires for team and bundle identifiers. Keep the reference to the driver's canonical `pluginId` constant so the switch cannot drift onto a nonexistent id. Gating a driver off still leaves its persisted active-plugin preference intact.

Preserved and hardened. `PluginCapability` stays a closed Swift enum with no raw-value or string construction, so an out-of-enum capability is a compile error rather than a runtime hope. No protocol in `PumpDriverAPI` exposes delivery, basal, or setting-write methods; calibrate, unpair, autoReconnectIfPaired and connect/disconnect remain classified as session/lifecycle, not therapy. Implement the follow-up Android recorded but never built: a CI lint that fails the build if a driver target writes to a known therapy control-point characteristic or exposes a symbol matching a delivery-verb denylist.

Ports verbatim as a compile-time Swift target and gains importance: with no Core Bluetooth in the Simulator it is the lead developer's only executable driver. Same id, name, version, and `{BGM_SOURCE, DATA_SYNC}` declaration — both multi-instance, deliberately never conflicting with a pump's GLUCOSE_SOURCE. Same lifecycle including the early return when `sim_enabled` is false and the resulting Disconnected sync card. The SupervisorJob scope becomes a `Task` retained by the driver and cancelled in onDeactivated and shutdown. Replace `println` with OSLog (no payloads).

Both cards port element-for-element: `demo-glucometer-status` at priority 100 with detail, the MUTED / ERROR<70 / WARNING>180 / SUCCESS LargeValue coloring, the Simulated INFO badge, the BATTERY+GLUCOSE IconValue row, the SparkLine, the battery ProgressBar; `demo-glucometer-sync` at priority 110 with last-sync HH:mm:ss in the system zone or the no-data string. The 5-second repaint becomes an AsyncStream with `Task.sleep(for: .seconds(5))` suspended when the view is off screen via `.task` — a battery win over Android's unconditional loop. All three settings sections port unchanged.

Same cardId gate, same 3-second rebuild, same layout: Recent Readings placeholder or the last 10 reversed as HH:mm:ss with mg/dL, SparkLine at history>=2, Manual Entry TextInput plus PRIMARY ActionButton, Simulator Controls repeating the toggle and slider, Safety Info showing live limits. The action reads `detail_bg_value`, parses with `Int(_:)`, publishes NewBgmReading with meterName 'Demo Glucometer (manual)', and clears the field. Fix two Android defects during the port: validate against the current SafetyLimits rather than the raw literal, and show an inline error instead of a silent no-op.

An `actor` producing a cold `AsyncStream<BgmReading>`. Generator ports exactly: base = 130 + 50·sin(phase), jitter +/-10, phase advanced by 2pi/12 for a 12-reading cycle, result rounded and clamped to 20...500. Critically the safety-limits read stays inside the loop, one `.value` per iteration — this is the reference behavior every real driver must copy. Out-of-range values are dropped, not clamped, and the delay still runs so cadence is unaffected by filtering. Both history arrays trimmed to 12; actor isolation replaces the informal one-collector-only rule.

needs_redesign.why: Three Android assumptions break. (1) `address: String` is a MAC on Android; iOS never exposes a BLE MAC — a peripheral is identified by `CBPeripheral.identifier`, a UUID that is app-specific, device-specific and NOT stable across app reinstall. (2) CoreBluetooth's `connect(_:options:)` has no timeout at all and retries indefinitely, including across app suspension and relaunch — the opposite of Android's documented 30s convention. (3) `scanForPeripherals(withServices: nil)` discovers nothing while the app is backgrounded; background scans must pass explicit service UUIDs and always coalesce duplicates, and only UUID-filtered scans are restored after a background relaunch. Medtronic's 'ignores address entirely' case is unaffected.
options: Keep `address: String` and carry `CBPeripheral.identifier.uuidString` in it — minimal API churn, but the field silently changes meaning and stops being reinstall-stable
Introduce a `DeviceIdentity` value type (opaque platform id + advertised name + optional pump serial) and re-bind on serial match when the UUID misses, so reinstall does not force a full re-pair

Split connect into `connect(identity:config:)` with a driver-owned timeout Task for user-initiated pairing, plus `awaitConnection(identity:)` that deliberately leaves the CoreBluetooth connect pending forever to power background reconnect
needs_redesign.recommendation: Adopt DeviceIdentity and both connect forms. Use a driver-owned 30s timeout for user-initiated connect to preserve the Android contract, and the never-timing-out pending connect for auto-reconnect — that is CoreBluetooth's designed reconnect path and is strictly better than Android's backoff loop. `scan()` must always pass the driver's service UUID set; unfiltered scan becomes a documented foreground-only debug affordance. Keep `config` as a free-form string map with `pairingCode` preserved.

needs_redesign.why: The 7 states port, but iOS adds two conditions the enum cannot express. First, `CBManagerState` (poweredOff, unauthorized, unsupported, resetting) is a first-class, user-actionable condition: connect() cannot even be attempted and there is no state to show — Android reaches the same situation by a different path and the enum papers over it. Second, Core Bluetooth state restoration relaunches the app straight into an already-connected peripheral without passing through SCANNING/CONNECTING/AUTHENTICATING; `willRestoreState` fires before `centralManagerDidUpdateState`, in a short background window, and cannot resume arbitrary driver work — the driver must rebuild session and auth context from persisted credentials.
options: Add cases to ConnectionState (`unavailable`, `unauthorized`, `restoring`) — simple, but mutates an enum shared with the watch target and the backend contract
Keep the 7 states and expose a parallel `bluetoothAvailability` stream on the registry, mirroring how PairingFault already runs parallel to ConnectionState
Model restoration as a synthetic transition — enter AUTHENTICATING, then CONNECTED or AUTH_FAILED — so no consumer ever observes a state it cannot interpret
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 2 plus option 3's synthetic transition, with no new public case. Keep the 7 names and the StateFlow-always-has-a-value guarantee for cross-platform parity, add the parallel availability stream (the PairingFault precedent is exactly this pattern), and emit synthetic transitions on restoration. AUTH_FAILED stays terminal-ish, requiring an explicit new connect(); explicit disconnect and give-up still land on DISCONNECTED.

needs_redesign.capability: PairingProfile / PairingStyle / PairingFault — the ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT path
needs_redesign.why: CENTRAL_SCAN (Tandem) is fine. ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT (Medtronic MiniMed 700-series) collides with two hard CoreBluetooth rules. When backgrounded, `CBPeripheralManager` drops `CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey` entirely and moves service UUIDs into the overflow advertising area, discoverable only by iOS devices explicitly scanning for that UUID — a pump scanning by name will never see a backgrounded iPhone. And `advertisedName` is only settable in the foreground advertisement payload; the GAP Device Name a pump may actually read is the user's device name ('Dan's iPhone'), which an app cannot set. iOS also cannot clear a BLE bond programmatically.
options: Foreground-only pairing: a modal pairing screen that advertises with a local name, explicit keep-this-screen-open instruction, and `isIdleTimerDisabled` while advertising
Instruct the user to rename their iPhone in Settings so the system device name matches what the pump expects, with an on-screen verification of the current name
Ship Medtronic gated off at launch using the existing feature gate and enable it only after advertise-and-wait is validated on Daniel's hardware
needs_redesign.recommendation: Options 1 and 3 together, with 2 documented as the fallback. Implement the foreground-only pairing modal, keep `PairingProfile.advertisedName` as the displayed expectation, and extend PairingFault with iOS-specific cases — `bluetoothUnauthorized`, `bluetoothPoweredOff`, `backgroundAdvertisingNameless` — alongside the existing five. PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED maps to `CBPeripheralManager.state == .unsupported`; ADVERTISE_FAILED to a failed `startAdvertising` callback; BOUND_ELSEWHERE stays the same heuristic timeout with no protocol signal.

needs_redesign.capability: Device discovery models and Tandem model detection
needs_redesign.why: `TandemPumpModel.fromAdvertisedName` ports verbatim — `CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey` yields the same advertised string, and the whitespace-collapse, case-insensitive prefix match, empty-string and 'Tandem Pump' fallback-to-UNKNOWN behaviors are all unchanged, tests included. What breaks is `DiscoveredDevice.address` and the legacy `DiscoveredPump`: no MAC, a per-install UUID, and RSSI only available at discovery time (a connected peripheral requires an explicit `readRSSI()`, so `rssi` must stay optional and the legacy `rssi ?: 0` coercion becomes actively misleading).
options: Store `CBPeripheral.identifier.uuidString` in `address` and accept a forced re-pair after every reinstall or device migration
Store the UUID plus the pump serial number read post-connect from Device Information Service / PumpHardwareInfo, and re-bind on serial match when the UUID misses
Drop the legacy `DiscoveredPump` shape entirely during the port rather than carrying its rssi coercion forward
needs_redesign.recommendation: Options 2 and 3. Persisting the serial alongside the peripheral UUID is what makes 'you reinstalled, we found your pump again' possible; without it, every reinstall or bundle-identifier change forces a full re-pair, which for Tandem means re-entering the pump pairing code from the pump screen. Delete DiscoveredPump. Keep the `metadata: [String: String]` bag on DiscoveredDevice for driver-specific advertisement data.

needs_redesign.why: Both shipped drivers poll every 60,000 ms in an unbounded loop. iOS has no foreground service and suspends the app between Core Bluetooth callbacks: a self-scheduled Timer or `Task.sleep` does not fire while suspended, and BGAppRefreshTask cannot be scheduled tighter than roughly 15 minutes — opportunistic, system-decided, not guaranteed. Holding an open BLE connection wakes the app for peripheral events, not for its own timers. So an exact 60s cadence is achievable only in the foreground. Worse, the Android implementations swallow failures via success-only handling, so on iOS an indefinitely stale display would be indistinguishable from a quiet pump.
options: Notification-driven: subscribe to the pump's CGM characteristic and let value-update callbacks wake the app — only works where the pump pushes, and Medtronic's own KDoc says its stream is polling, not pump-pushed
Hybrid: exact 60s cadence in the foreground; in the background rely on connection and notification wakes plus history-log backfill on the next wake to close every gap
Register BGAppRefreshTask and BGProcessingTask as opportunistic supplements, and use BGContinuedProcessingTask for a user-initiated full history backfill with a system progress UI
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 2 as the architecture with option 3 as a supplement, and move cadence ownership out of the capability into a platform polling orchestrator — where Medtronic's KDoc already says it is headed. Explicitly do NOT port the swallow-failures behavior: surface poll failure and last-successful-read time, because iOS will produce far more gaps than Android and staleness must be visible rather than inferred.

needs_redesign.capability: PumpStatus capability — unpair(), autoReconnectIfPaired(), and full history sync
needs_redesign.why: The six read methods and the three pure `extract*` functions port unchanged; drop-never-clamp is language-independent. Two lifecycle methods do not. An iOS app cannot remove a Bluetooth bond — only the user can, via Settings > Bluetooth > Forget This Device — so `unpair()` can clear credentials and disconnect but may leave a stale bond that blocks re-pairing with a fresh key. `autoReconnectIfPaired()` maps far better on iOS than Android because an indefinite pending connect plus state restoration does the work, so its shape should change too. Both currently sit on PUMP_STATUS, meaning a device driver without PUMP_STATUS has no unpair path at all.
options: Make `unpair()` async, clear app-side credentials, cancel the connection, and return a flag telling the UI to instruct the user to also forget the device in iOS Settings
Make both methods `async throws` now — the Android TODO says exactly this, and the port is the free moment to do it
Move both from PUMP_STATUS to DevicePlugin, fixing the Android quirk that a device driver without PUMP_STATUS has neither unpair nor reconnect
needs_redesign.recommendation: All three. `unpair()` becomes `async throws -> UnpairResult` carrying `requiresSystemForget: Bool`; both lifecycle methods move to DevicePlugin where they belong. Keep `getFullHistoryLogs`'s defaulted delegation to `getHistoryLogs` (Tandem overrides, Medtronic does not) and run the unbounded variant under BGContinuedProcessingTask so a long Tandem backfill survives backgrounding. Fix the KDoc property names (glucoseLow/glucoseHigh/maxBolus do not exist) rather than porting them.

needs_redesign.why: Half of this capability disappears: the runtime path — no-arg constructor plus reflective instantiation from a sideloaded DEX JAR — is impossible on iOS. The compile-time path also has no direct equivalent: Swift and SPM have no Hilt `@Binds @IntoSet` multibinding, and Swift cannot enumerate types conforming to a protocol at runtime. Drivers must be registered in an explicit, hand-maintained list, which introduces a failure mode Android does not have: a driver that compiles but was never added to the list is silently absent from the app.
options: A single `DriverCatalog.all: [any PluginFactory]` array in the app module, hand-maintained
An SPM build-tool plugin that scans driver targets with SwiftSyntax and generates the registration array at build time
Each driver package exposes a `register(into:)` entry point called from one explicit place, with a test asserting the catalog's exact expected set of plugin IDs
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 1 plus option 3's test. The driver set is small and fixed, and a codegen build plugin adds complexity to a repo every user must build themselves. `metadata` stays available without instantiation as a `static var` on the factory type so the settings screen can list drivers without creating them, and the platform — not the factory — still calls `initialize(context)` with the same context instance handed to `create`.

needs_redesign.why: The struct ports trivially, but the version check changes meaning. On Android it is a runtime gate rejecting a mismatched sideloaded JAR; with compile-time linking a driver can never be older than the app it is built into, so a runtime `apiVersion != 5` check is dead code. Its real iOS value is as a source-compatibility marker for out-of-tree forks carrying a private driver. This is also the moment to resolve the three-way drift — code says 5, docs/dev/plugin-architecture.md says 2, and the example README and META-INF/plugin.json say 1, which is why the shipped example would be rejected today.
options: Keep the runtime check as belt-and-braces — cheap, but it always passes
Move enforcement to build time: an XCTest asserting every registered factory's apiVersion equals PLUGIN_API_VERSION, so a stale out-of-tree driver fails CI instead of silently vanishing at runtime
Drop the constant and rely purely on SPM semantic versioning of the PumpDriverAPI package
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 2 plus SPM semver on PumpDriverAPI, bumping major on breaking changes to Plugin/DevicePlugin, capability protocols, PluginContext parameters, PluginEvent cases, or descriptor cases — the same rule Android documents. Set the Swift constant to 5 and fix all three documentation sites in the same change; do not carry the drift into the new repo. Keep the reverse-domain plugin-ID regex and the 'Tandem v1.0.0' protocolName+version rendering convention.

needs_redesign.capability: Deprecated pump interfaces (PumpDriver, PumpConnectionManager, PumpScanner, HistoryLogParser) and their registry adapters
needs_redesign.why: These four interfaces plus four adapters exist purely to keep pre-plugin Android call sites compiling. A green-field Swift port has no such call sites, so porting them imports roughly eight types of pure technical debt — including two genuine defects. HistoryLogParserAdapter returns an empty list when no pump plugin is active, indistinguishable from 'no new records', which masks data loss; and the deprecated `limits: SafetyLimits = SafetyLimits()` default parameters silently substitute absolute limits whenever a caller forgets to pass the user's narrowed configuration.
options: Port all four plus adapters for line-by-line traceability against the Android source
Port none; every iOS call site goes directly to the registry's capability slots
Port none, but keep the adapters' one good behavior — an explicit no-active-plugin error rather than an empty or substituted result
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 3. Delete the deprecated surface entirely, and make 'no active pump plugin' a typed error everywhere — never an empty array, never a default-constructed SafetyLimits. Also delete the `SafetyLimits()` default parameter from every signature so the user's configured limits must be passed explicitly; that default is a latent safety bug rather than a convenience, and the port is the only cheap moment to remove it.

needs_redesign.capability: Safety-constant drift guard (the 20..500 bound duplicated across ~15 sites)
needs_redesign.why: The Android guard works three ways, the third being a comment-stripped source scan for inline `20..500` literals across modules a test cannot import. That third mechanism is fragile, and the port is the moment to remove the need for it. Separately, the Android repo's static-analysis gates lean on Semgrep's Kotlin and Java rulesets, which have no Swift equivalent, so 'the same security testing in substance' must be reconstructed from different tools rather than by copying the workflow.
options: Reproduce the Android guard verbatim in XCTest including a source scan over the driver sources

Consolidate to one `GlucoseBounds.absolute: ClosedRange<Int> = 20...500` in a SafetyCore module referenced by CgmReading, BgmReading, SafetyLimits, CalibrationTarget, PluginEvent, the watch target and the widget, plus a SwiftLint custom rule banning bare `20...500` and `20..<501` outside that file
Both: consolidate, and keep a reduced guard test asserting the constants and exercising every validator at its boundaries
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 3, and state the security-gate mapping plainly rather than by tool name. Semgrep parses Swift but there is no Swift security ruleset comparable to p/kotlin or p/java; the substance is recovered from MobSF for iOS/Swift static analysis, `xcodebuild analyze` (Clang static analyzer), SwiftLint custom rules encoding this project's own invariants, and Periphery for dead code. Language-agnostic gates port by name unchanged: gitleaks/trufflehog for secrets, zizmor for GitHub Actions, osv-scanner for Package.resolved (thinner Swift coverage than Maven — supplement with Dependabot's SPM support).

needs_redesign.capability: Fidelity of the example driver as a reference
needs_redesign.why: On Android the demo plugin is a nice-to-have; on iOS it becomes load-bearing. Core Bluetooth does not exist in the iOS Simulator, and the lead developer has no iPhone and no Apple Watch, so every non-hardware validation runs in the Simulator. But the Android demo is a plain Plugin, not a DevicePlugin: no connect/disconnect/scan, no ConnectionState, no PairingProfile or PairingFault, no credential use, no DebugLogger, no CalibrationTarget participation, and no capability entry for its declared DATA_SYNC. Those are precisely the surfaces most in need of Simulator exercise.
options: Port the demo as-is and accept that the entire DevicePlugin surface is untestable without Daniel's hardware

Add a `SimulatedPumpDriver` implementing the full DevicePlugin + PumpStatus + InsulinSource + GlucoseSource + CalibrationTarget surface with scriptable scenarios: connect, auth failure, link loss, reconnect, restoration entry, occlusion, partial delivery, out-of-range readings, and both pairing styles including advertise-and-wait faults

Add a recorded-trace replay driver that plays captured Tandem and Medtronic packet logs through the real parsers so extract* and the drop-never-clamp filters run against real wire data in the Simulator
needs_redesign.recommendation: Options 2 and 3, both shipped in the repo and both runnable in the Simulator and in CI. The scriptable simulator is how the connection state machine, pairing faults, restoration and safety filtering get automated coverage; the trace-replay driver is how parser correctness gets covered without a pump. Also fix the demo's apiVersion inconsistency and its use of the raw 20...500 literal instead of the configured limits.

needs_redesign.why: Nothing here survives literally: Gradle modules, compileSdk 35 / minSdk 30, jvmTarget 17, ProGuard consumer rules, the Gradle lockfile, kotlinx-coroutines exported as an api dependency, and the d8 DEX packaging step all disappear. The fork-and-build distribution model adds constraints Android does not have: bundle identifiers, App Group identifiers and Keychain access groups must be templated per user because every fork signs with a different Team ID, and the proguard keep-rules for capability reflection have no analogue because Swift capability lookup is not reflective.
options: One Xcode project with targets — simplest for a fork-and-build user, weakest module boundary

SPM packages for SafetyCore, PumpDriverAPI and one per driver, consumed by a thin app target — real internal/package access boundaries, which is what replaces Kotlin `internal` for the platform-only event bypass
Mixed: SPM for the API and drivers, an Xcode project for the app, watch app and widget extension
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 3. Pin Swift and Xcode versions in the CI workflow and in a `.xcode-version` file, and commit `Package.resolved` as the lockfile equivalent. SafetyCore must build for iOS, watchOS and the widget extension so no surface outside the phone app can construct an invalid reading. Templated TEAM_ID, BUNDLE_ID_PREFIX and APP_GROUP live in an xcconfig the forking user fills in once, following the Loop/LoopWorkspace pattern.

impossible.capability: Runtime plugin loading (DEX JAR sideloading via DexPluginLoader)
impossible.why: iOS forbids executing code that is not present in the signed app bundle. There is no DexClassLoader equivalent, `dlopen` of a downloaded binary is blocked by code signing and by App Store and TestFlight policy, and Swift has no reflective instantiation of a class named by a manifest string. Every element of this capability is unimplementable: the DexClassLoader with the app classloader as parent, the 65,536-char-bounded META-INF/plugin.json read, `loadClass(factoryClass).getConstructor().newInstance()`, the PluginFactory cast, and the exact-match apiVersion rejection.
impossible.closest_alternative: Compile-time-linked driver targets — already the decided architecture — plus the fork-and-build distribution model as the authorship path: a third-party driver author forks the repo, adds a Swift package target conforming to DevicePlugin, registers it in DriverCatalog, and the user builds and signs it into their own TestFlight. The PluginManifest fields (id, name, version, apiVersion, factoryClass, author, description) survive as static metadata on the factory type, validated by the same reverse-domain ID regex and by a build-time apiVersion assertion instead of a runtime rejection. The trust step moves from 'user taps install and accepts a warning' to 'user builds with their own signing key'.

impossible.why: With no runtime loading there is nothing to install. The entire mechanism is Android-specific plumbing for a capability iOS does not have: the Storage Access Framework document picker, the .jar suffix requirement, filename sanitization, the canonical-path traversal guard with its trailing-separator refinement, the 50 MB streaming abort, the PK\x03\x04 ZIP magic check, `setReadOnly()` for DexClassLoader, and the setWritable-then-delete removal. iOS also gives a user no supported way to place an executable artifact into an app's container.
impossible.closest_alternative: Nothing user-facing survives. The equivalent trust decision moves to build time and becomes visible in the repository: which drivers a given fork links is declared in DriverCatalog and in the xcconfig feature flags. The one thing worth keeping in spirit is the security warning — the pre-build documentation and the in-app driver list should state which drivers are compiled into this build and that they were reviewed as source rather than contained at runtime.

impossible.why: RestrictedContext is a ContextWrapper that throws SecurityException for roughly thirty Context operations and allowlists seven system services. iOS has no per-module runtime capability restriction: all code in an app bundle shares one sandbox, one entitlement set, one container and one Keychain. Swift cannot deny one target access to CoreBluetooth, the file system or URLSession at runtime, and there is no getSystemService chokepoint to allowlist. The stated design philosophy — that safety enforcement comes from backend-synced SafetyLimits rather than blanket Context restriction — is the part that does survive intact.
impossible.closest_alternative: Compile-time containment in place of runtime containment: each driver lives in its own SPM target declaring only SafetyCore, PumpDriverAPI and CoreBluetooth as dependencies, so importing UIKit, URLSession or app internals is a build error rather than a caught SecurityException; back that with a CI lint over driver-target imports and a CODEOWNERS review gate on driver code. ScopedCredentialProvider's deliberate unencrypted-SharedPreferences compromise disappears entirely — on iOS every driver uses the same Keychain-backed store, which is strictly stronger than the Android runtime-plugin path and removes that documented revisit trigger.

ios_requirements: The app must define the absolute glucose validity range 20-500 mg/dL exactly once, in a module shared by the phone app, the watch app and any widget extension, and every reading model, safety-limit type, calibration validator and event validator must reference that single definition.

CI must fail the build if the glucose bounds, the mmol/mg-dL factor 18.0156, or the Tandem epoch offset 1199145600 drifts from its canonical value, and must exercise every validator at both its accept and reject boundaries.

Every reading model (CGM, BGM, bolus) must reject out-of-range construction by throwing, so a driver cannot publish an unvalidated value and a caller that omits filtering fails loudly rather than storing bad data.

All history extraction and bolus-history paths must drop out-of-range readings and doses rather than clamp them, and tests must prove that a 900 mg/dL record and a 40 U bolus are absent from the result rather than coerced to 500 and 25.
Drivers must read the current safety limits at every validation pass, and a test must prove that narrowing the limits mid-stream changes which readings are accepted without restarting the driver.

The app must accept safety limits only from backend sync and must never offer a local override; limits received from the backend must be clamped rather than crash the app, and any clamping must be recorded and surfaced.
The app must expose the age of the last safety-limit sync and must treat a never-synced install as stale.
A user must be able to see every pump driver compiled into their build, which drivers are active, and which capability slot each one occupies.
Activating a driver must never leave its capability slot empty during the swap, and activating a conflicting single-instance driver must automatically deactivate the previous one.
Deactivating a driver must stop its work while preserving its credentials and settings, so reactivation does not require re-pairing.

A maintainer must be able to disable a specific driver at build time such that it is absent from the driver list, never instantiated and never polled, while the user's prior selection is preserved for when it is re-enabled.

A user must be able to pair a Tandem t:slim X2 by scanning, choosing from a device list and entering the pump pairing code, with model-appropriate instructions derived from the advertised name and generic instructions for an unrecognized model.

A user must be able to pair a Medtronic 700-series pump by keeping a pairing screen open while the phone advertises, selecting the phone from the pump's own menu, and must be shown a specific reason when the attempt stalls: Bluetooth off, Bluetooth permission denied, this device cannot advertise, advertising rejected, handshake timed out, authentication rejected, or the pump is still bound to another phone.
The app must reconnect automatically to a previously paired pump after being backgrounded, after being terminated by the system, and after device reboot, without the user reopening the app.
The app must remain able to identify a previously paired pump after the app is reinstalled or the phone is replaced, or must clearly tell the user that re-pairing is required and why.
When a user unpairs a pump the app must clear its stored credentials and disconnect, and must tell the user when an additional Forget This Device step in iOS Settings is required to complete removal.
The app must distinguish 'no new reading' from 'the pump has not responded', and must surface the age of the most recent successful read rather than presenting an indefinitely stale value as current.
The app must backfill pump history after any period of lost connectivity or app suspension, and a full history sync started by the user must be able to continue while the app is backgrounded.
Pump credentials and pairing codes must be stored encrypted, unavailable before first device unlock, excluded from iCloud and encrypted backups, and removed when the app is deleted and reinstalled.
Raw BLE packet payloads must be retained only in debug builds and only in memory, and must never be written to any log or file that can leave the device.

The app must expose no insulin delivery, basal change or pump setting write anywhere in the driver API, and CI must fail if a driver introduces a write to a therapy control point or a symbol matching a delivery-verb denylist.

The app must ship a fully simulated pump driver, runnable in the iOS Simulator without Bluetooth, that exercises connection, authentication failure, link loss, reconnection, background restoration, both pairing styles, every pairing fault, and out-of-range readings.
The app must ship a recorded-trace replay driver so that real Tandem and Medtronic packet parsing and safety filtering can be validated in the Simulator without a physical pump.

A user must be able to fork the repository, supply their own Apple Team ID and App Store Connect API key, and produce a signed TestFlight build through GitHub Actions without owning a Mac and without any project-published binary.

The app must declare NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription and the bluetooth-central and bluetooth-peripheral background modes, and must degrade to a clearly labelled unavailable state when Bluetooth is off, unauthorized or unsupported.

Every driver plugin ID must match the reverse-domain identifier pattern and every settings key must match the settings-key pattern, enforced at build time, because both values are also persistence keys.
Event delivery between drivers and the platform must be explicitly best-effort with bounded buffering, and no user-facing alerting may depend on it for a delivery guarantee.
A driver that is compiled into the app but not registered in the driver catalog must fail CI rather than be silently absent from the running app.

risks.risk: The 60-second glucose poll cannot run on schedule while the app is backgrounded. iOS suspends the app between Core Bluetooth callbacks so a self-scheduled timer does not fire, and BGAppRefreshTask is opportunistic at roughly 15-minute-or-worse granularity. Android's foreground service has no iOS equivalent, so iOS users will see data gaps Android users do not.
risks.mitigation: Drive cadence from peripheral notifications where the pump pushes; hold an indefinite pending connect so link events wake the app; backfill every gap from history logs on the next wake; and surface last-successful-read age prominently so a gap is visible rather than a stale number presented as current. Move cadence ownership from the capability into a platform polling orchestrator.

risks.risk: Medtronic advertise-and-wait pairing may be unachievable in the background and unreliable even in the foreground: iOS drops the advertised local name when the app is backgrounded and never lets an app set the system GAP device name. If the pump matches on device name rather than the advertisement local name, the flow cannot work without the user renaming their iPhone.
risks.mitigation: Implement foreground-only pairing with a keep-awake modal and explicit on-screen instructions, ship Medtronic behind the existing feature gate, and enable it only after validation on Daniel's hardware. Document the rename-your-iPhone fallback and detect the mismatch on screen.

risks.risk: Nothing BLE is testable in the iOS Simulator and the lead developer has neither an iPhone nor an Apple Watch. Every connection, pairing, authentication, restoration and reconnection path depends on one maintainer's devices for validation, making that maintainer a single point of failure in the release pipeline.
risks.mitigation: Make the scriptable simulated driver and the trace-replay driver first-class shipped targets with CI coverage rather than test fixtures. Define a hardware smoke-test checklist Daniel runs before each tagged release, and treat any change to driver connection or authentication code as requiring hardware sign-off.

risks.risk: Peripheral identity is not stable on iOS: CBPeripheral.identifier is per-app-install, so reinstalling the app, rebuilding a fork with a different bundle identifier, or moving to a new phone silently loses the pairing binding — and for Tandem that means re-entering the pump pairing code from the pump screen.
risks.mitigation: Persist the pump serial number alongside the peripheral UUID and re-bind on serial match. Keep Keychain items in a stable access group keyed off a templated identifier so an in-place rebuild does not orphan credentials, and purge orphaned Keychain items only on a genuine fresh install.

risks.risk: Medtronic's bolus cursor is process-local, unpersisted, and advances before the orchestrator persists — tolerable on Android because the durable Room-backed slow loop self-heals. iOS suspends and terminates apps far more aggressively, so the fast path will skip boluses much more often, and porting it without the durable path would lose insulin records.
risks.mitigation: Persist the cursor, and do not ship the fast path until durable per-sequence history persistence exists. Make the durable path the source of truth for insulin totals and treat the cursor path strictly as a latency optimization.

risks.risk: Critical Alerts is the only iOS mechanism that breaks through Silent mode and Focus, and its entitlement is granted by Apple only on individual request against a specific Team ID. In a fork-and-build model where every user signs with their own personal developer account, that entitlement is not obtainable, so no urgent-low alarm can be guaranteed to sound.
risks.mitigation: Use Time Sensitive notifications, whose entitlement is available to every developer without approval, plus a Live Activity for continuous glucose display, and state the limitation plainly in onboarding and the medical disclaimer: this app is not an alarm system. Coordinate with the alerting subsystem owner — this cannot be solved inside the driver API.

risks.risk: Removing the runtime plugin loader deletes a real Android capability (third-party driver authorship without a repo change), and removing RestrictedContext deletes the only runtime containment for driver code. On iOS every compiled-in driver has the app's full entitlements, container and Keychain.
risks.mitigation: Replace runtime containment with build-time containment: per-driver SPM targets declaring minimal dependencies, a CI import lint, CODEOWNERS review on driver targets, and an in-app list stating which drivers are compiled in. Document 'fork, add a target, build with your own key' as the supported authorship path.

risks.risk: Core Bluetooth state restoration relaunches the app directly into a connected peripheral, bypassing SCANNING, CONNECTING and AUTHENTICATING, and gives only a short window in which willRestoreState fires before the manager state callback. A driver that assumes it always enters through connect() will observe an inconsistent state machine or fail to re-establish its authenticated session.
risks.mitigation: Require every DevicePlugin to implement an explicit restoration entry point that rebuilds session and authentication context from persisted credentials, and emit synthetic AUTHENTICATING then CONNECTED or AUTH_FAILED transitions so downstream consumers never see an unreachable state. Cover restoration explicitly in the simulated driver's scenario set.

risks.risk: Swift cannot enumerate protocol conformances at runtime, so a driver that compiles but is never added to the registration catalog is silently absent from the app — a failure mode Hilt's @IntoSet multibinding prevents on Android.
risks.mitigation: A CI test asserting the catalog contains exactly the expected set of plugin IDs, updated deliberately whenever a driver is added, renamed or gated.

risks.risk: UserDefaults returns a zero value rather than throwing when a key is read with the wrong typed accessor, converting Android's loud ClassCastException into a silent wrong value — which for a settings key feeding a threshold would be a wrong number rather than a crash.
risks.mitigation: Maintain a per-driver key-to-type table asserted in tests, and never let a driver-owned settings value participate in glucose or dose validation; validation limits come only from the backend-synced SafetyLimits.

risks.risk: safeOf can silently produce a 1 mg/dL-wide accept window from a nonsensical backend config (min 450, max 300 yields 450-451), after which nearly every reading is dropped and the app appears to have lost the pump with no explanation.
risks.mitigation: Log and surface every clamping event, and add a sanity check that reports a resulting window narrower than a configurable floor to the user and to telemetry as a configuration fault rather than silently accepting it.

risks.risk: Activation intentionally calls onActivated on the new driver before deactivating the conflicting one, so two drivers transiently hold the same single-instance capability and both can publish readings. A naive Swift port using a reentrant actor can widen that window from milliseconds to an unbounded await.
risks.mitigation: Keep the registry on the main actor with a serialized activation queue rather than a reentrant actor, and tag events with the publishing driver so duplicates during the overlap are detectable downstream.

risks.risk: Semgrep's Kotlin and Java security rulesets that back the Android repo's static gates have no Swift equivalent, so a naive port of the CI configuration would report green while testing nothing.
risks.mitigation: Reconstruct the substance with MobSF, xcodebuild analyze, SwiftLint custom rules encoding this project's own safety invariants, and Periphery; carry gitleaks, zizmor and osv-scanner across unchanged; and record in the CI documentation which Android gate each Swift gate replaces.

risks.risk: The Android source carries a three-way PLUGIN_API_VERSION inconsistency (code 5, architecture doc 2, example manifest 1) and PumpStatus KDoc references SafetyLimits property names that do not exist. Porting from the documentation rather than the code would encode wrong contracts into the new repository.
risks.mitigation: Treat the Kotlin source as the sole authority for the port, and land the documentation corrections in the Android repo in the same change set so the two repositories do not diverge further.

questions_for_pm: Medtronic 700-series pairing requires the phone to advertise as a BLE peripheral under a name the pump can recognize, and iOS strips the advertised name whenever the app is backgrounded and never lets an app set the system-level device name. That makes Medtronic pairing foreground-only at best, and possibly dependent on the user renaming their iPhone. Is a foreground-only, instruction-heavy Medtronic pairing flow acceptable as parity, or should Medtronic ship gated off on iOS until hardware validation proves the flow works end to end?
